definition_zh: v. 围攻，围困（城镇、要塞）；团团围住；使应接不暇
definition_en: to surround a place with an army in order to capture it; to crowd around someone closely; to overwhelm someone with demands
core_image: 城墙外层层扎营的帐篷，把一座城连水带粮一起掐断
scene: 敌军在城外扎营三个月，切断了所有补给。The enemy army besieged the town for three months, cutting off every supply line.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：besiege 指军队围攻城镇；句意是敌军围城三个月，切断了一切补给。

senses.title: To surround a place with an army
senses.definition: to surround a town or fortress with armed forces so that nothing can get in or out
senses.definitionCN: 以武装力量包围城镇或要塞，使人无法进出
senses.example: Supply wagons never reached the walls while the city was besieged.
senses.exampleCN: 城池被围期间，补给车始终没能抵达城下。
senses.why: Siege first meant a seat, the place an army set itself down in front of a wall.
senses.whyCN: siege 最初意为「座位」，即军队在城墙前安营落座之处。

senses.title: To crowd around someone
senses.definition: to press closely around a person or place, as a crowd does
senses.definitionCN: 像人群那样紧紧围住某人或某处
senses.example: Fans besieged the singer the moment she stepped out.
senses.exampleCN: 歌手一走出来，粉丝就把她团团围住。
senses.why: A crowd around a person looks like an army around a town, so the military image transfers to daily life.
senses.whyCN: 把人群围住某人想成军队围城，军事意象就自然转到日常生活。

senses.title: To overwhelm with requests
senses.definition: to overwhelm someone with questions, letters or demands
senses.definitionCN: 用问题、来信或要求把人淹没
senses.example: The office was besieged with complaints after the change.
senses.exampleCN: 改版之后，办公室被投诉淹没了。
senses.why: The sense of the walls being pressed from outside becomes mental: requests crowd the mind with no gap.
senses.whyCN: 城墙被从外面挤压的感觉变成心理上的：请求密密麻麻，毫无缝隙。

intro.en: Besiege is the prefix be- laid over siege, a word that began as the seat an army takes in front of a wall.
intro.cn: besiege 是前缀 be- 加在 siege 上，而 siege 原本指军队在城墙前「落座」的地方。

items.en: Latin sedere means to sit, the root behind siege and session.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为「坐」，是 siege 与 session 的共同词根。

items.en: Old French siege means a seat, then the place where an army sits down.
items.cn: 古法语 siege 意为座位，后指军队安营落座之处。

items.en: English siege names the act of sitting down before a fortified place.
items.cn: 英语 siege 指在设防之地前「坐定」围困。

items.en: Adding be- makes a verb: to put an army all around the walls.
items.cn: 加上 be- 构成动词：把军队布满城墙四周。

items.en: The verb extends to crowds that press around a person.
items.cn: 该动词扩展到把某人团团围住的人群。

items.en: Modern usage adds the sense of being flooded with demands.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上「被要求淹没」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps other be- verbs so the prefix pattern stays in view; the near-meaning group moves from the physical ring to the abstract pressure.
note.cn: 形近组保留其他 be- 动词，让前缀规律一直可见；近义组由实体的包围圈走到抽象的压力。

normal.cn: siege 意为座位，围城就是军队在城墙外坐下不走。

normal.en: Be- means all around, so be-siege is sitting all around the town.

normal.en: The tents do not move until the bread runs out.

normal.en: A crowd around a celebrity copies the same ring of tents.

normal.en: Being besieged with letters feels like walls closing in.

abstract.en: A ring drawn in the dust that nothing may cross.
abstract.cn: 在尘土里画下的一个圈，任何东西都不得穿过。

abstract.en: Patience used as a weapon against a gate.
abstract.cn: 把耐心当作攻门的武器。

abstract.en: Attention pressed from every side until there is no gap left.
abstract.cn: 四面压来的目光，直到不留一丝缝隙。

examples.en: The city was besieged for two years before it fell.
examples.cn: 这座城被围困两年才陷落。

examples.en: Reporters besieged her as she left the courtroom.
examples.cn: 她离开法庭时，记者把她团团围住。

examples.en: The helpline was besieged with calls after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后，求助热线被电话淹没。

definition_zh: 打赌；赌注；（口语）敢说
definition_en: to risk money on a result, or the money risked
core_image: 赛马场边攥着票根的手
scene: 他攥着票根盯住冲过终点的马。He bet ten pounds on the black horse.
sceneCN: 这里 bet 是「打赌」（第 1 个义项：拿钱押在某结果上）；句意是他押了十英镑在那匹黑马上。

derivatives.zh: 由 bet 加 -ing 构成，义为「赌博」
由 bet 加 -or 构成，义为「下注者」

senses.title: To risk money on a result
senses.definition: to risk money on the result of an event
senses.definitionCN: 拿钱押在某事的结果上
senses.example: He bet ten pounds on the black horse.
senses.exampleCN: 他押了十英镑在那匹黑马上。
senses.why: This is the core sense, tied to racing and cards.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，与赛马和纸牌紧密相关。

senses.title: The money risked
senses.definition: the money or thing risked in a bet
senses.definitionCN: 下注时押上的钱或物
senses.example: He lost the bet and paid at once.
senses.exampleCN: 他赌输了，当场付了钱。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the stake itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词转作名词，指押上的赌注。

senses.title: To feel sure
senses.definition: to say that one is sure about something
senses.definitionCN: 表示对某事很有把握
senses.example: I bet she will call tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我敢说她今晚会打电话来。
senses.why: Everyday speech loosened betting into a confident guess.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把「下注」放宽为有把握的猜测。

intro.cn: bet 在十六世纪进入英语，确切来源不明。

items.cn: you bet 成为热烈的「当然」。

items.en: I bet marked a strong guess.

definition_zh: v. 背叛，出卖（朋友、国家、信任）；泄露，流露出（情绪、秘密）
definition_en: to be disloyal to someone who trusts you; to reveal a feeling or secret without meaning to
core_image: 一张递出去的地图，把背后那扇暗门的位置指给了敌人
scene: 他把部队的行军路线交给了对面，换回一袋钱。He betrayed the route of the march to the other side for a bag of coins.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：betray 指出卖信任自己的人；句意是他为了一袋钱把行军路线卖给了对面。

senses.title: To be disloyal to a trust
senses.definition: to act against someone who trusts you, usually for your own gain
senses.definitionCN: 为自身利益做出违背他人信任的事
senses.example: He betrayed the men who had hidden him.
senses.exampleCN: 他出卖了那些藏匿过他的人。
senses.why: The Latin root tradere means to hand over, and a traitor hands a person over to an enemy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 tradere 意为「交出」，叛徒就是把某人交到敌人手上。

senses.title: To give away a secret
senses.definition: to reveal something that was meant to stay hidden
senses.definitionCN: 把本应隐藏的事透露出去
senses.example: One careless word betrayed the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不慎的话泄露了整个计划。
senses.why: Handing over a secret is the same gesture as handing over a person, so the sense widens from people to information.
senses.whyCN: 交出秘密与交出人本是同一个动作，于是词义由人扩展到信息。

senses.title: To show a feeling unintentionally
senses.definition: to make a feeling visible even when you try to hide it
senses.definitionCN: 即使想掩饰也让情绪显露出来
senses.example: Her voice betrayed how tired she was.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音泄露了她有多疲惫。
senses.why: The face hands over what the mouth denies, so the verb comes to mean an involuntary reveal.
senses.whyCN: 脸上交出了嘴上否认的东西，于是这个词表示不由自主的显露。

intro.en: Betray comes from Latin tradere, to hand over, by way of Old French trahir; the be- is English.

items.en: English betray adds be- to the French verb.

items.en: The verb extends from people to secrets that are given away.

items.en: Later usage covers feelings that show despite concealment.
items.cn: 后世用法涵盖掩饰不住而显露的情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps be- verbs for the prefix shape; the near-meaning group separates the disloyal act from the mere leaking of information.

abstract.en: The body confessing what the mouth denies.

examples.en: He betrayed no sign of surprise.

examples.en: She felt betrayed by the people she had trusted.

examples.en: The way he avoided her eyes betrayed his guilt.
examples.cn: 他躲闪的目光泄露了他的愧疚。

scene: 服务员把咖啡、果汁和别的饮料一并摆上桌。The waiter set out coffee, juice and every other beverage the guests might want.

senses.title: A drink other than water
senses.definition: a liquid made for drinking, usually other than plain water
senses.definitionCN: 供饮用的液体，通常指水以外的饮品
senses.example: Tea is the most common hot beverage in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 茶是办公室里最常见的热饮。
senses.why: Beverage comes from Latin bibere, to drink, and simply names anything drinkable.
senses.whyCN: beverage 源自拉丁语 bibere（喝），就是「可饮之物」的统称。

senses.title: A drink served on a formal occasion
senses.definition: a drink offered at a meal, reception or public event
senses.definitionCN: 在餐会、招待会或公共活动中提供的饮品
senses.example: The hotel charges extra for beverages at conferences.
senses.exampleCN: 会议期间酒店对饮品另行收费。
senses.why: On menus and signs the word sounds formal, so it clusters around catered events.
senses.whyCN: 在菜单与标牌上这个词显得正式，因此常出现在供餐场合。

intro.en: Beverage goes back to Latin bibere, to drink, through Old French bevrage.

items.en: Bibere means to drink, the source of beverage and bibulous.

items.en: The past participle bibitum means having been drunk.
items.cn: 过去分词 bibitum 意为「已被喝下」。

items.en: Old French bevrage names a drink or a serving of drink.
items.cn: 古法语 bevrage 指饮品或一份饮料。

items.en: English borrows the word as a general term for drink.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，作「饮品」的通称。

items.en: Menus and inn signs give the word its formal tone.
items.cn: 菜单与旅店招牌赋予这个词正式色彩。

items.en: The word heads a whole industry of bottled and canned drinks.
items.cn: 这个词统领了整个瓶装罐装饮料产业。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bever- stem or its Latin origin; the near-meaning group runs from the plainest word for a drink to the formal words for what is served.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bever- 词干或其拉丁来源；近义组由最朴素的「喝的东西」走到正式场合的说法。

entries.definitionCN: 据说有魔力的一剂饮液。

normalIntro.en: Bibere is Latin for drink, and beverage is the formal English heir of that word.
normalIntro.cn: bibere 是拉丁语的「喝」，beverage 就是它在英语里的正式后代。

normal.en: Beverage and bibulous share the Latin verb to drink.
normal.cn: beverage 与 bibulous 共用那个拉丁语「喝」。

normal.en: Think of a bevvy, slang for a drink.
normal.cn: 想想 bevvy，俚语里的「一杯」。

normal.en: Anything on a tray that is not water is a beverage.
normal.cn: 托盘上除水以外的东西都是 beverage。

normal.en: Menus say beverage where friends say drink.
normal.cn: 菜单说 beverage，朋友之间说 drink。

normal.en: Latin bibere left its b and v marks in the word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 bibere 在词里留下了 b 与 v 的痕迹。

abstract.en: A drink that arrives with a menu, not a tap.
abstract.cn: 随菜单而非水龙头而来的饮品。

abstract.en: Liquid arranged for guests.
abstract.cn: 为客人摆好的液体。

abstract.en: Thirst handled politely.
abstract.cn: 被礼貌地处理的口渴。

examples.en: The room rate includes a hot beverage at breakfast.
examples.cn: 房价包含早餐的一份热饮。

examples.en: Please keep beverages away from the keyboards.
examples.cn: 请让饮料远离键盘。

examples.en: The beverage industry spends millions on packaging.
examples.cn: 饮料业在包装上花费数百万。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「杯勿惹」——杯子里的饮料别乱碰，洒在键盘上就麻烦了。

root: 古法语 bevrage ← 拉丁 bibere（喝）+ -age（名词后缀）

sensesIntro.en: The word names a drink in two registers: anything drinkable, and specifically what a host or a venue puts on the table.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词在两个层面指饮品：一切可饮之物，以及主人家或场所摆上桌的那一份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tray of glasses with water beading on the sides
core.cn: 核心意象：托盘上排开的玻璃杯，杯壁挂着水珠

branches.en: A cup of tea on a desk.
A bottle of juice in a fridge.
A glass passed round at a reception.
branches.cn: 招待会上传了一圈的杯子。

branches.en: A price list of drinks at a conference.
Anything poured that is not water.

intro.en: Beverage is a French noun on the Latin verb for drinking; the endings below build the vocabulary of drinks and the act of drinking.
intro.cn: beverage 是建立在拉丁语「喝」之上的法语名词；下面这些词缀构成饮品与饮酒行为的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin bibere means to drink, potare to drink deeply, and haurire to draw up liquid.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bibere 意为喝，potare 意为痛饮，haurire 意为汲取液体。

latinEntries.exampleCN: bibere 产生 beverage 与 bibulous。
potare 是 potion 的来源。
haurire 产生 exhaust。

definition_zh: v. 当心，谨防（常用于警示）；提防某人或某物
definition_en: to be careful of something dangerous; used especially in warnings
core_image: 栅栏上挂着一块歪斜的木牌，上面只写着两个字：当心
scene: 栅栏上挂着一块木牌，提醒过路人当心那条狗。A board on the fence reminded passers-by to beware of the dog.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：beware 用于提醒人提防危险；句意是栅栏上的木牌提醒路人当心那条狗。

senses.title: To be on guard against danger
senses.definition: to be careful because something may be dangerous or harmful
senses.definitionCN: 因某物可能危险有害而小心
senses.example: Beware of the edge; the path crumbles there.
senses.exampleCN: 当心那处边缘，小路在那里塌了。
senses.why: Beware began as be ware, two words meaning be watchful.
senses.whyCN: beware 起初写作 be ware，两个词，意为「保持警觉」。

senses.title: To be cautious about a person
senses.definition: to treat a person with suspicion because they may deceive you
senses.definitionCN: 因对方可能欺骗而对其保持戒心
senses.example: Beware of anyone who offers a deal too good to be true.
senses.exampleCN: 要提防那些开出好得不像真的条件的人。
senses.why: The same watchfulness turns from a cliff edge to a human character.
senses.whyCN: 同一份警觉，从悬崖边转向人的品性。

intro.en: Beware was once two words, be ware, an order to stay watchful like a sentry.
intro.cn: beware 原本是两个词 be ware，是一句像哨兵口令般的「保持警觉」。

items.en: Old English waer means watchful and cautious.
items.cn: 古英语 waer 意为警觉、谨慎。

items.en: Beon is the verb to be, here used as a command.
items.cn: beon 是动词「是」，此处作命令式。

items.en: The phrase be ware is spoken as a warning to look out.
items.cn: 短语 be ware 作为「留神」的警告使用。

items.en: The two words merge into a single verb.
items.cn: 两个词合并成一个动词。

items.en: The word settles into notices such as beware of the dog.
items.cn: 这个词固定出现在「当心恶犬」一类告示上。

items.en: Beware usually stands alone or takes of before its object.
items.cn: 现代用法中 beware 常单独使用，宾语前加 of。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps be- verbs; the near-meaning group layers the alarm from a quiet adjective to a shouted command.
note.cn: 形近组保留 be- 动词；近义组把警报从安静的形容词排到喊出的命令。

entries.definition: To happen to someone, usually badly.
To surround a place with an army.
To watch over and protect something.

normalIntro.en: Beware is simply be ware, be watchful, so the warning is built into the spelling.
normalIntro.cn: beware 就是 be ware，保持警觉，警告的意思直接写在拼写里。

normal.en: Split it: be ware, meaning be watchful.
normal.cn: 拆开看：be ware，意思是保持警觉。

normal.en: Ware is the same watchful root as wary.
normal.cn: ware 与 wary 同出「警觉」一词根。

normal.en: A sentry saying be ware is saying beware.
normal.cn: 哨兵喊 be ware，就是在喊 beware。

normal.en: Wooden signs all over the world say beware of the dog.
normal.cn: 全世界的木牌上都写着当心恶犬。

normal.en: Where there is a warning, the word is beware.
normal.cn: 哪里有警示，哪里就有 beware。

abstract.en: A hand held up before a step.
abstract.cn: 迈步之前举起的一只手。

abstract.en: Attention paid in advance of harm.
abstract.cn: 在伤害到来之前付出的注意。

abstract.en: The cheapest form of protection.
abstract.cn: 最廉价的防护。

examples.en: Beware of the dog, the gate does not latch.
examples.cn: 当心这条狗，大门关不严。

examples.en: Travellers were told to beware of pickpockets in the square.
examples.cn: 旅客被告知在广场上要当心扒手。

examples.en: Beware, the roads freeze early on this hill.
examples.cn: 当心，这座山的道路结冰很早。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「别忘」——出门前别忘了提醒自己一句：当心。

root: be（是，保持）+ ware（警觉的）→ 保持警觉，即当心

sensesIntro.en: One watchfulness covers two objects: a dangerous thing in front of you and a dangerous person beside you.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一份警觉对准两类对象：眼前的危险之物，以及身边的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crooked wooden board nailed to a fence, with two words of warning on it
core.cn: 核心意象：钉在栅栏上的一块歪木牌，上面只有两个字：当心

branches.en: A cliff edge marked with a rope.
branches.cn: 用绳子圈出的悬崖边缘。

branches.en: A sign above a wet floor.
A smile that arrives too quickly.
A contract with a missing page.

branches.cn: 在任何事发生之前就付出的小心。

intro.en: Beware joins the verb be with the old adjective ware; the endings below build the vocabulary of watchfulness and warning.
intro.cn: beware 由动词 be 与古形容词 ware 合成；下面这些词缀构成警觉与警告的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin vigilare means to stay awake on watch, cavere to take care, and monere to warn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vigilare 意为守夜不眠，cavere 意为当心，monere 意为警告。

latinEntries.meaning: to take care, to be on guard
latinEntries.exampleCN: cavere 产生 caution 与 caveat。
vigilare 产生 vigil 与 vigilant。
monere 产生 monitor 与 admonish。

definition_zh: 使迷惑；使不知所措；使晕头转向；把……弄糊涂；使混乱
definition_en: to confuse someone completely, so they cannot think clearly or find their way
core_image: 走岔路口的旅人：路标全转了个圈，四顾茫然
scene: 列车晚点，站内的指示牌又七零八落。The complicated map bewildered the first-time visitors.
sceneCN: 这里 bewilder 是「使迷惑、使不知所措」（第 1 个义项：令人 confused 得晕头转向）；句意是复杂的地图让初次来访的游客晕头转向。

collocations.zh: 令人眼花缭乱的一大堆

derivatives.zh: 过去分词转形容词，义为「困惑的；不知所措的」
现在分词转形容词，义为「令人困惑的；眼花缭乱的」
bewilder 加名词后缀 -ment，义为「困惑；迷乱」
基础词，义为「荒野的；狂乱的」，bewilder 由其派生
同源名词，义为「荒野」，其古义「迷路的荒地」是 bewilder 的源头

senses.title: To confuse completely
senses.definition: to make someone so confused that they cannot think or act clearly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人困惑到无法清晰思考或行动
senses.example: The complicated map bewildered the first-time visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 复杂的地图让初次来访的游客晕头转向。
senses.why: The old image is losing one's way in the wilderness, now in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 古义是在荒野中迷路，如今转为心智上的迷失。

senses.title: To leave someone at a loss
senses.definition: to make someone feel helpless because they do not know what to do
senses.definitionCN: 因不知该如何应对而令人手足无措
senses.example: She was bewildered by the sudden accusations.
senses.exampleCN: 突如其来的指责让她不知所措。
senses.why: A lost traveler stands still, unsure which step to take.
senses.whyCN: 迷途的旅人原地呆立，不知下一步迈向何处。

senses.title: To make something puzzling
senses.definition: to make a system, rule, or situation too tangled to follow
senses.definitionCN: 使制度、规则或情形盘根错节而难以理解
senses.example: A bewildering array of choices faced the buyer.
senses.exampleCN: 琳琅满目的选择令买家眼花缭乱。
senses.why: Many tangled paths make a forest bewildering.
senses.whyCN: 岔路繁多，森林便令人迷乱。

senses.title: To confuse the senses
senses.definition: to overload sight, sound, or smell so that the senses lose order
senses.definitionCN: 让视觉、听觉或嗅觉过载，感官失去条理
senses.example: The market's noise and colours bewildered his senses.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的喧嚣与色彩让他的感官应接不暇。
senses.why: The wilderness image applies to perception as well as thought.
senses.whyCN: 荒野迷路的意象同样适用于感官层面。

senses.title: To disorder or jumble
senses.definition: to throw something into confusion or disorder
senses.definitionCN: 使某物陷入混乱无序
senses.example: The contradictory reports bewildered the investigation.
senses.exampleCN: 互相矛盾的报告搅乱了调查。
senses.why: To bewilder an order is to make paths cross without signposts.
senses.whyCN: 打乱秩序，就是让路径交错而无路标可循。

senses.title: To perplex mentally
senses.definition: to puzzle someone's mind over a question or idea
senses.definitionCN: 以问题或想法难住某人的头脑
senses.example: The geometry proof bewildered the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 这道几何证明难住了全班。
senses.why: A mind, like a traveler, can lose the logical path.
senses.whyCN: 头脑如旅人，也会在逻辑之路上迷路。

senses.title: To disorient in place
senses.definition: to make someone lose their sense of direction or place
senses.definitionCN: 使某人失去方向感或方位感
senses.example: The mirrored corridors bewildered the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 镜子迷宫般的走廊让客人们晕头转向。
senses.why: This keeps the original literal sense of wandering lost.
senses.whyCN: 此义保留了字面上「迷路」的本义。

senses.title: To stun with novelty
senses.definition: to overwhelm someone with things too new or rapid to absorb
senses.definitionCN: 以过于新奇或迅疾的事物将人淹没
senses.example: The pace of change bewildered the older workers.
senses.exampleCN: 变化的节奏令老员工目不暇接。
senses.why: When new paths appear faster than one can walk, one is lost again.
senses.whyCN: 新路出现得比脚步更快，人便再度迷失。

intro.en: Bewilder is be- plus an old verb wilder, to lead astray, from wilderness.
intro.cn: bewilder 由 be- 加古动词 wilder「使迷路」构成，wildler 源自 wilderness「荒野」。

items.en: wildēor meant wild beast; wild dēor, wild animal, the source of wilderness.
items.cn: 古英语 wildēor 意为「野兽」，wild dēor 即 wild animal，是 wilderness 的来源。

items.en: wildernesse meant a wild, pathless place where one wanders lost.
items.cn: 中古英语 wildernesse 指无路的荒野，人在其中迷途彷徨。

items.en: wilder meant to lead astray, to lure into the wilds; origin partly uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 wilder 意为「使迷路、引入荒野」；其来源部分不确定。

items.en: bewilder first appears meaning to lose one's way in pathless places.
items.cn: 17 世纪晚期 bewilder 首见，义为在无路之地迷失。

items.en: now chiefly figurative: to confuse the mind, the senses, or the plans.
items.cn: 如今多作比喻：使心智、感官或计划陷于迷乱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the wild and wilderness roots; the near-meaning group gathers confusing words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 wild 与 wilderness 词根；近义组汇集「使困惑」类词。

entries.definitionCN: 野的；狂乱的——bewilder 的词基
困惑；迷乱——bewilder 的派生名词
使困惑——侧重问题复杂难解

entries.definition: to mix up in the mind
to cause to lose sense of direction
entries.definitionCN: 使迷失方向——侧重空间方位

normalIntro.en: Bewilder is be- plus wilder: led into the wilds and lost.
normalIntro.cn: bewilder 是 be- 加 wilder：被引入荒野而迷路。

normal.en: Wilderness is the picture behind the word.
normal.cn: 荒野是这个词背后的画面。

normal.en: The common pattern is be bewildered by.
normal.cn: 常用句式是 be bewildered by。

normal.en: Bewildering describes the confusing thing.
normal.cn: bewildering 形容令人困惑之物。

normal.en: Bewilderment is the state of confusion.
normal.cn: bewilderment 指困惑的状态。

normal.en: It first meant losing one's way literally.
normal.cn: 它最初指字面上的迷路。

abstract.en: See signposts spinning until none points true.
abstract.cn: 看路标纷纷打转，没有一个指对方向。

abstract.en: Feel the forest close where the path vanished.
abstract.cn: 感受小径消失后森林合拢。

abstract.en: Picture a dozen doors opening at once, all wrong.
abstract.cn: 想象十扇门同时打开，扇扇都错。

examples.en: The complicated map bewildered the first-time visitors.
examples.cn: 复杂的地图让初次来访的游客晕头转向。

examples.en: She was bewildered by the sudden accusations.
examples.cn: 突如其来的指责让她不知所措。

examples.en: A bewildering array of choices faced the buyer.
examples.cn: 琳琅满目的选择令买家眼花缭乱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「比·外的」——路标全是「比外围还外」的陌生岔道，看得人晕头转向。

root: 前缀 be-（古英语，表「使陷入」）加 wilder（中古英语动词「使迷路」，一般认为源自 wilderness；wilderness 由古英语 wild dēor「野兽」复合而来，更早词形存疑）；17 世纪晚期 bewilder 义为「在荒野迷路」，现代英语主要作比喻的「使迷惑」。

sensesIntro.en: A lost traveler in pathless wilds gives English its word for every modern kind of confusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 「无路荒野中的迷途者」为英语提供了从迷路到一切现代困惑的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveler surrounded by trackless wilds
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人被无路的荒野包围

intro.en: Bewilder is a Germanic be- verb on the wild root.

latinIntro.en: No Latin kin; the wild family is purely Germanic.

definition_zh: 在……那边；超出；迟于
definition_en: on the other side of something, or more than a limit
core_image: 越过山脊后展开的陌生平原
scene: 翻过山脊，眼前展开一片陌生平原。The village lies beyond the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 beyond 是「在……那边」（第 1 个义项：位于某物的另一侧）；句意是村庄在山的那一边。

derivatives.zh: 语义关联词，义为「超过」，对应 beyond 的越界含义

senses.title: On the other side
senses.definition: on the far side of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的另一侧
senses.example: The village lies beyond the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 村庄在山的那一边。
senses.why: This is the oldest spatial sense, looking past a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的空间义，视线越过一条界线。

senses.title: More than a limit
senses.definition: greater than a limit or ability
senses.definitionCN: 超过某个限度或能力
senses.example: The price is beyond our budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这个价格超出了我们的预算。
senses.why: Crossing a physical line became crossing any limit.
senses.whyCN: 越过实际的界线，引申为越过任何限度。

senses.title: Later than a point in time
senses.definition: later than a stated time
senses.definitionCN: 晚于某个时间点
senses.example: Do not stay out beyond ten.
senses.exampleCN: 十点以后别待在外面。
senses.why: Time was treated as a line that can be crossed.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作一条可以越过的线。

items.en: beyond covers space, limits and time.

normalIntro.en: Beyond means on the far side, past a line you can see.

normal.en: Beyond the hills means on the far side.

normal.en: Beyond belief means too strange to accept.

normal.en: Beyond control means no one can stop it.
normal.cn: beyond control 指无法控制。

normal.en: Beyond doubt means certainly true.
normal.cn: beyond doubt 指毫无疑问。

normal.en: The word is fixed in form.

examples.cn: 十点以后别待在外面。

sensesIntro.en: Space, limit and time each have a line that beyond crosses.

definition_zh: 偏见；偏向；偏差；使有偏见
definition_en: an unfair preference or a systematic slant in judgment, data, or design, or to influence something unfairly
core_image: 保龄球被做偏的一侧：球滚着滚着自己拐向一边
scene: 研究发布前，审稿人反复追问样本来源是否站得住脚。The study was criticized for a bias that favoured the sponsor's product.
sceneCN: 这里 bias 是「研究中的系统性偏差」（第 2 个义项：数据或方法偏向一方）；句意：这项研究因偏向赞助商产品而受到批评。场景要点：研究报告、赞助商标志、一边倒的数据图表。

collocations.zh: 斜着；沿斜纹方向（裁剪用语）

senses.title: Prejudice for or against a group
senses.titleCN: 偏见：对某群体先有立场
senses.definition: an unfair preference or dislike for a person or group based on identity rather than evidence
senses.definitionCN: 基于身份而非证据，对某人或某群体不公平的偏好或厌恶
senses.example: The hiring panel was accused of gender bias.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘小组被指存在性别偏见。
senses.why: The original bias was a weight placed off-centre on a bowling ball. The ball therefore curves one way; a mind with bias curves toward one group.
senses.whyCN: 最初的 bias 是保龄球上偏置的配重。球因此向一边拐；有 bias 的心也会向某个群体拐。

senses.title: Systematic distortion in data or research
senses.titleCN: 系统性偏差：数据整体偏了一边
senses.definition: a systematic error that makes results consistently differ from the truth in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 使结果持续朝一个方向偏离真实情况的系统性误差
senses.example: The survey suffered from selection bias because it only reached smartphone users.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查存在选择偏差，因为它只触及智能手机用户。
senses.why: A bowling ball with an off-centre weight does not make random errors; it curves the same way every time. Statistical bias is that consistent curve.
senses.whyCN: 偏置配重的保龄球不是随机出错，而是每次都朝同一边弯。统计偏差就是这种持续一致的弯曲。

senses.title: A personal leaning or tendency
senses.titleCN: 个人偏向：心里更倾向某一边
senses.definition: a preference or inclination that shapes how someone thinks or acts
senses.definitionCN: 影响一个人思考或行动方式的偏好或倾向
senses.example: He has a bias for simple solutions over complicated ones.
senses.exampleCN: 他偏向简单方案，而不是复杂方案。
senses.why: The curve need not be hostile; any off-centre weight makes the ball drift. In the same way, a mild preference is already a bias.
senses.whyCN: 这种弯曲不必带敌意；只要配重偏离中心，球就会漂。同样，温和的偏好也已经是一种 bias。

senses.title: An oblique line or grain
senses.titleCN: 斜线：布料或裁剪的斜向
senses.definition: a slanting direction, especially the diagonal grain of woven fabric or a cut made across it
senses.definitionCN: 倾斜的方向，尤指织物的斜纹或横过布纹的裁剪
senses.example: The dress was cut on the bias so that it would drape softly.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子沿斜纹裁剪，因此垂坠柔和。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense: biais in Old French meant 'slant, oblique'. The line runs across the straight grain.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的实体义：古法语 biais 就是“倾斜、斜的”。这条线横过笔直的布纹。

senses.title: To influence unfairly
senses.titleCN: 使有偏见：把判断推向一边
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to favour one side unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某事物不公平地偏向一边
senses.example: The editor was accused of biasing the report against the opposition.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑被指让报道对反对派产生偏见。
senses.why: The verb applies the off-centre weight: a force is added to one side, so the result rolls that way.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是加上偏置配重：往一边施力，结果便朝那边滚。

senses.title: Electronics: a steady voltage or current
senses.titleCN: 电子学：偏置电压或电流
senses.definition: a fixed voltage or current applied to a device to set its operating point
senses.definitionCN: 施加于器件、用来设定其工作点的固定电压或电流
senses.example: The transistor needs a small bias voltage to conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 晶体管需要一个小偏置电压才能导通。
senses.why: The electrical sense keeps the geometry: the operating point is pushed away from the centre to one side so the device responds correctly.
senses.whyCN: 电子义保留了这种几何：工作点被从中心推向一边，器件才能正确响应。

senses.title: Cognitive bias
senses.titleCN: 认知偏误：思维自己走捷径
senses.definition: in psychology, a repeatable pattern in which judgment departs from logic or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中判断反复偏离逻辑或证据的模式
senses.example: Confirmation bias makes people notice evidence that supports what they already believe.
senses.exampleCN: 确认偏误使人更容易注意到支持自己既有信念的证据。
senses.why: The mind's default path is the off-centre weight. It saves effort but curves every judgment in the same direction.
senses.whyCN: 心智的默认路径就是那块偏置配重。它省力，却让每个判断都朝同一方向弯。

senses.title: Algorithmic or AI bias
senses.titleCN: 算法偏见：模型学进了偏差
senses.definition: a systematic unfairness in a model or system, usually learned from biased data or design choices
senses.definitionCN: 模型或系统中系统性的不公平，通常来自有偏差的数据或设计选择
senses.example: The chatbot showed bias because its training data underrepresented certain dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 这个聊天机器人表现出偏见，因为训练数据对某些方言代表性不足。
senses.why: A model repeats the curve it was trained on. If the data leaned one way, the machine leans the same way at scale.
senses.whyCN: 模型会重复它被训练时见到的弯曲。数据偏向一边，机器就会大规模地朝同一边偏。

senses.title: Media bias
senses.titleCN: 媒体偏向：报道框架有倾斜
senses.definition: a tendency in news reporting to present events from one perspective or to favour one side
senses.definitionCN: 新闻报道倾向于从某一视角呈现事件或偏袒某一方
senses.example: Readers complained about the paper's political bias.
senses.exampleCN: 读者抱怨这家报纸有政治偏向。
senses.why: Selection and framing act like an off-centre weight on the whole report: some facts are pushed forward, others are pushed out of view.
senses.whyCN: 选择与框架就像给整篇报道加了偏置配重：有些事实被推向前面，另一些被推出视野。

intro.en: Bias began as a word for a slanting line and became the name of a weighted bowling ball. From that curved roll came the modern senses of prejudice and systematic distortion.
intro.cn: bias 最初指一条斜线，后来成为偏置保龄球的名称。从那种弯曲的滚动，长出了现代“偏见”和“系统性偏差”的含义。

items.en: Bias enters English in the 1520s as 'an oblique or diagonal line'. The earliest uses are about cuts, slopes, and geometry.
items.cn: bias 在 1520 年代进入英语，意为“斜线、对角线”。最早用法与裁剪、斜面、几何有关。

items.en: By the 1560s a bias was also a weight placed on one side of a bowling ball so that it curved as it rolled. The bowl had a bias; the path showed it.
items.cn: 到 1560 年代，bias 也指保龄球一侧的配重，使球滚动时弯曲。球本身“有 bias”，轨迹把这一点显示出来。

items.en: The English word comes from Old French biais 'slant, slope, oblique'. French already used it for both a diagonal line and a leaning tendency.
items.cn: 英语这个词来自古法语 biais“倾斜、斜面、斜的”。法语中它已经既指斜线，也指倾向。

items.en: The deeper origin of biais is not settled. One suggestion traces it through Vulgar Latin *(e)bigassius to Greek epikarsios 'athwart, crosswise', from epi- 'upon' + karsios 'oblique'; this is a hypothesis, not an attested chain.
items.cn: biais 更深层的来源尚无定论。一种说法认为它经通俗拉丁语 *(e)bigassius 追溯到希腊语 epikarsios“横向的、斜穿过去的”，由 epi-“在上”+ karsios“斜的”构成；这只是假说，不是有文献链的结论。

items.en: By the 1570s bias was used for a leaning of the mind. A ball that curves became a judgment that curves; the weight moved from the bowl to the person.
items.cn: 到 1570 年代，bias 被用于表示心智的倾向。会弯的球变成了会弯的判断；配重从球上移到了人身上。

items.en: Statistics, psychology, electronics, media studies, and AI all use the same geometry: a system pushed off-centre, so that its output consistently leans one way.
items.cn: 统计学、心理学、电子学、媒体研究和人工智能都使用同一种几何：系统被推离中心，于是输出持续偏向一边。

note.en: The first group is built on the same bias; the second collects words for unfair leaning, each naming a different kind of tilt.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个 bias 上；第二组收“不公平倾向”的词，各自命名不同类型的倾斜。

entries.definition: showing an unfair preference. It is the past participle of bias used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出不公平偏好的。它是 bias 的过去分词转作形容词。

entries.definition: fair and without preference. Un- 'not' + biased removes the off-centre weight.
entries.definitionCN: 公正、无偏好的。un-“不”+ biased，去掉偏置配重。

entries.definition: plural of bias, or the third-person singular of the verb. It is not a different root.
entries.definitionCN: bias 的复数，或动词第三人称单数。它不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: an opinion formed before knowing the facts, especially about a group. It is usually social and emotional; bias can be statistical and neutral in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 在了解事实之前形成的看法，尤指对某群体。它通常带社会性和情绪性；bias 可以是统计性的、语气中性的。

entries.definition: unfair support for one person or side. It stresses favouring a particular party rather than a distorted system.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某一方的不公平支持。它强调偏袒特定一方，而不是系统被扭曲。

entries.definition: a particular point of view imposed on information, or a sloping direction. Slant is often used for media framing.
entries.definitionCN: 强加于信息的特定视角，或倾斜方向。slant 常用于媒体框架。

entries.definition: a general inclination to behave in a certain way. It is broader and can be neutral, while bias implies unfairness in most modern uses.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式行事的一般倾向。它更宽泛，可以中性；bias 在现代用法中多含不公平意味。

normalIntro.en: Real image and relatives: a bowling ball with an off-centre weight, the adjective biased, and the modern debias.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实意象与同族词：一侧加配重的保龄球、形容词 biased，以及现代词 debias。

normal.en: A bowling ball with a weight on one side curves as it rolls. That curve is the original bias.
normal.cn: 一侧加配重的保龄球滚起来会弯。那道弯曲就是最初的 bias。

normal.en: Biased is the adjective: a biased report has a weight on one side of its scale.
normal.cn: biased 是形容词：a biased report 的天平一侧被加了重量。

normal.en: Unbiased removes the weight, so the result can roll straight.
normal.cn: unbiased 去掉了那块配重，结果才能直着滚。

normal.en: To debias a model is to find and remove the off-centre weight in its training data.
normal.cn: debias 一个模型，就是找出并移除训练数据里的偏置配重。

normal.en: On the bias means diagonally across the grain of cloth, the oldest concrete sense.
normal.cn: on the bias 指沿斜纹横过布纹，这是最古老的实体义。

abstract.en: Bias is not the same as being wrong. It is a consistent direction of error, like a ball that always curves left.
abstract.cn: bias 不等于“错了”，而是一种持续一致的错误方向，像永远向左弯的球。

abstract.en: The weight can sit in a person, a dataset, a question, a newsroom, or a circuit. The geometry is identical.
abstract.cn: 配重可以放在一个人、一份数据、一道问题、一间新闻编辑室或一个电路里。几何关系完全相同。

abstract.en: Removing bias is not the same as having no perspective; it means no hidden weight is steering the result without being declared.
abstract.cn: 消除 bias 不等于没有视角；它意味着没有隐藏的配重在不声明的情况下操纵结果。

examples.en: The judge was asked to step aside because of a perceived bias.
examples.cn: 由于被认为存在偏见，法官被要求回避。

examples.en: The test was redesigned to remove cultural bias.
examples.cn: 这项测试被重新设计，以消除文化偏差。

examples.en: Social media algorithms can amplify political bias.
examples.cn: 社交媒体算法会放大政治偏向。

dict_mnemonic.text: “拜厄斯”——拜厄斯看人总先挑一边站，像偏心的保龄球 → bias 偏见、偏向

root: 源自古法语 biais“倾斜、斜面”；最初指斜线，16 世纪又指保龄球一侧的配重，球因此弯曲滚动，核心是“偏离中心、持续倒向一边”。更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of bias, all built on one geometry: a weight placed off-centre, making the path curve consistently toward one side.
sensesIntro.cn: bias 的九个义项都建立在同一种几何上：配重偏离中心，使路径持续朝一边弯曲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an off-centre weight that makes a ball, a judgment, or a system lean one way.
core.cn: 核心意象：偏离中心的配重，让球、判断或系统倒向一边。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND MEDIA LEANING: prejudice toward a group, a personal preference, a newsroom's framing.
branches.cn: 社会与媒体倾向：对群体的偏见、个人偏好、新闻编辑室的框架。

branches.en: SYSTEMATIC ERROR: selection bias, cognitive shortcuts, and learned algorithmic unfairness.
branches.cn: 系统性误差：选择偏差、认知捷径，以及算法学到的系统性不公。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: the original slant of a line or the diagonal grain of cloth.
branches.cn: 几何：最初的斜线，或布料的斜纹。

branches.en: THE VERB: to add the off-centre weight and push a result toward one side.
branches.cn: 动词：加上偏置配重，把结果推向一边。

branches.en: ELECTRONICS: a fixed voltage that sets an operating point away from centre.
branches.cn: 电子学：把工作点设定在偏离中心的固定电压。

intro.en: Bias is a borrowed French noun. English adds -ed, un-, -es, and -ing; modern technical English coins de- and -free compounds.
intro.cn: bias 是借入的法语名词。英语加 -ed、un-、-es、-ing；现代技术英语又造出 de- 和 -free 复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable classical Latin word for bias. The suggested Vulgar Latin *(e)bigassius, linked to Greek epikarsios, is a hypothesis, so latinEntries is left empty rather than presenting a speculative root as fact.
latinIntro.cn: bias 没有可靠的古典拉丁语来源。所谓的通俗拉丁语 *(e)bigassius（与希腊语 epikarsios 相联系）只是假说，因此 latinEntries 留空，不把推测词根当作事实。

items.meaning: more than one bias, or 'it biases'
items.meaningCN: 多种偏见；或动词第三人称单数
items.example: The report identifies several hidden biases.
items.exampleCN: 报告指出了几处隐藏的偏见。

items.meaningCN: 有偏见的；偏向的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The sample was biased toward younger voters.

items.meaningCN: 无偏见的；公正的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: We need an unbiased review of the evidence.
items.exampleCN: 我们需要对证据进行公正的审查。

items.meaningCN: 使产生偏向；正在加偏置（-ing 构成分词）
items.example: The wording of the question was biasing the answers.
items.exampleCN: 问题的措辞正在使答案产生偏向。

items.meaning: the same as biasing, with doubled s
items.meaningCN: 与 biasing 同义，英式拼写双写 s

items.meaning: to remove a known bias from data or a process
items.meaningCN: 去偏；从数据或流程中消除偏差（de- 表示去除）
items.example: The team tried to debias the training set.
items.exampleCN: 团队试图去除训练集的偏差。

items.example: Debiasing is easier when the source of the skew is known.
items.exampleCN: 当偏差来源已知时，去偏会更容易。

items.meaning: designed or tested to contain no bias
items.meaningCN: 无偏差的；无偏见的（free 表示“没有”）
items.example: The company promised a bias-free hiring process.
items.exampleCN: 公司承诺采用无偏见的招聘流程。

items.meaning: to apply excessive bias in electronics or modelling
items.meaningCN: 过偏；施加过大的偏置（over- 表示“过度”，技术用语）
items.example: The amplifier was overbiased and overheated.
items.exampleCN: 放大器偏置过大，导致过热。

definition_zh: 参考书目；文献目录；目录学；文献学
definition_en: a list of books or writings on a subject, or the study of such lists
core_image: 论文末页那一列列整齐的书名，像点名册
scene: 论文写完，导师只提醒别忘了列参考书。Her thesis included a bibliography of ninety titles.
sceneCN: 这里 bibliography 是「参考书目」（第 1 个义项：论文所引书籍的清单）；句意是她的论文附有九十种书目的参考清单。

derivatives.zh: bibliography 的形容词，义为「书目的；目录学的」
bibliography 加 -er，义为「目录学家；书目编制者」
同根词，义为「藏书癖；爱书癖」

senses.title: A list of books used or consulted
senses.definition: a list of the books and articles used in writing a work, placed at its end
senses.definitionCN: 著作末尾所列写作时引用或参考的书目清单
senses.example: Her thesis included a bibliography of ninety titles.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论文附有九十种书目的参考清单。
senses.why: Greek biblion means book and graphein means to write, so the word is a writing of books.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 biblion 指书，graphein 指书写，故该词本义是「写书之录」。

senses.title: A systematic catalog of writings
senses.definition: a complete or systematic list of writings on a given subject or by a given author
senses.definitionCN: 就某主题或某作者系统地编成的著作总目
senses.example: The library published a bibliography of local history writings.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆出版了本地历史著作的专题目录。
senses.why: Not just one essay's sources, but a field's whole book-list.
senses.whyCN: 不限于单篇的引用，而是一整领域的书总账。

senses.title: The study of books as objects
senses.definition: the scholarly study of the history and description of books, their printing and transmission
senses.definitionCN: 研究书籍的历史、版本、印刷与流传的学问
senses.example: Bibliography traces how the first edition changed hands.
senses.exampleCN: 目录学追踪初版的流传经过。
senses.why: Describing books systematically is itself a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 系统地为书立传，本身即一门学科。

senses.title: The description of textual variants
senses.definition: the branch that analyzes editions and textual differences among printings
senses.definitionCN: 分析版本及其文字差异的分支
senses.example: Analytical bibliography revealed two distinct printings.
senses.exampleCN: 分析目录学揭示出两种不同的印次。
senses.why: Comparing copies is the scholarly eye of bibliography.
senses.whyCN: 比对版本是目录学的学术之眼。

senses.title: A list at a chapter's end
senses.definition: a short reading list appended to a chapter or article for further reading
senses.definitionCN: 附于章节或文章末尾的延伸阅读书单
senses.example: Each chapter ends with a short bibliography.
senses.exampleCN: 每章末尾都附有简短的参考书目。
senses.why: The book-list shrinks to serve one section.
senses.whyCN: 书目清单缩小为服务单章。

senses.title: Works about a person's writings
senses.definition: a compilation of everything a particular author has written
senses.definitionCN: 汇集某位作者全部作品的目录
senses.example: The volume closes with a complete bibliography of her novels.
senses.exampleCN: 全书以她的小说完整目录作结。
senses.why: The book-list can center on one writer's output.
senses.whyCN: 书目也可以围绕一位作家的产出。

senses.title: Citation format rules
senses.definition: the conventions governing how books are cited and described
senses.definitionCN: 关于如何著录与引用书籍的规范
senses.example: The journal's bibliography style demands page numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊的著录格式要求标注页码。
senses.why: Writing-of-books implies rules for writing them down.
senses.whyCN: 「写书之录」自然包含记录的规则。

senses.title: The book trade's documentation
senses.definition: the record-keeping of publications for the book trade and libraries
senses.definitionCN: 为书业与图书馆所做的出版物登记记录
senses.example: National bibliography registers every new title in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 国家书目登记国内每一种新书。
senses.why: A country's whole output becomes one grand book-list.
senses.whyCN: 一国的出版总汇即一部大书目。

intro.en: Bibliography joins Greek biblion, book, and graphein, to write.
intro.cn: bibliography 由希腊语 biblion「书」加 graphein「书写」构成。

items.en: the root gwrebh- meant to scratch, to dig; source of graphein; reconstructed form.
items.cn: 词根 gwrebh- 意为「刻画、挖刻」，是 graphein 的来源（重构形式）。

items.en: biblion meant book, from Byblos, the Phoenician city of papyrus trade.
items.cn: 希腊语 biblion 意为「书」，源于以纸草贸易闻名的腓尼基城邦比布鲁斯。

items.en: bibliographia meant the writing of books, first of book-copyists' work.
items.cn: 希腊语 bibliographia 意为「关于书的书写」，最初指抄书人的工作。

items.en: bibliographia passed through Latin and French into European learned use.
items.cn: bibliographia 经拉丁语与法语进入欧洲学术用语。

items.en: English took it in the 17th century as the writing of books, then shifted to book-lists.
items.cn: 英语于 17 世纪借入，先指著书，后转为书目之义。

items.en: today it names both the reference list and the science of books.
items.cn: 如今既指参考书目，也指目录学。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the biblio- root; the near-meaning group gathers related scholarly lists.
note.cn: 形近组共享 biblio- 词根；近义组汇集学术清单类近义词。

entries.definition: the life story of a person
entries.definitionCN: 传记——拼写相近但词根不同（bio- 指生命）
目录——通用清单，不限于书

entries.definition: books assigned or recommended for reading
entries.definitionCN: 阅读书单——教学语境的书目

entries.definition: an alphabetical list at the end of a book
entries.definitionCN: 索引——按关键词而非书名编排

normalIntro.en: Bibliography is biblio- (book) plus -graphy (writing).
normalIntro.cn: bibliography 是 biblio-（书）加 -graphy（书写）。

normal.en: Biblion came from the city of Byblos.
normal.cn: biblion 源自城市比布鲁斯。

normal.en: An annotated bibliography adds notes.
normal.cn: annotated bibliography 附有注解。

normal.en: Bibliophile means a book lover.
normal.cn: bibliophile 指爱书人。

normal.en: The plural is bibliographies.
normal.cn: 复数是 bibliographies。

normal.en: It also names the study of books.
normal.cn: 它也指目录学。

abstract.en: See book spines marching in a neat queue.
abstract.cn: 看书脊排成一列整齐的队伍。

abstract.en: Feel the debt of every page to the books before it.
abstract.cn: 感受每页文字对前人书籍的致谢。

abstract.en: Picture a scholar naming books like honored guests.
abstract.cn: 想象学者如介绍贵宾般逐一报出书名。

examples.en: Her thesis included a bibliography of ninety titles.
examples.cn: 她的论文附有九十种书目的参考清单。

examples.en: Each chapter ends with a short bibliography.
examples.cn: 每章末尾都附有简短的参考书目。

examples.en: Bibliography traces how the first edition changed hands.
examples.cn: 目录学追踪初版的流传经过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必不里哦抄弗」——论文末必列书目，不抄不弗（不列），通不过。

root: 希腊语 biblion「书」（一般认为源自腓尼基城邦比布鲁斯 Byblos，纸草贸易之地）加 graphein「书写」（词根上溯至原始印欧语 gwrebh-「刻画」，重构形式）；bibliographia 原指抄书人之业，17 世纪进入英语，后转为「书目」与「目录学」。

sensesIntro.en: From writing about books, the word branches into lists, scholarship, citation rules, and national registers.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「写书之录」出发，词义分出清单、学问、著录规则与国家登记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the writing that names all the writings
core.cn: 核心意象：为所有书写立名的书写

intro.en: Bibliography is a Greek compound of book and writing.
intro.cn: bibliography 是「书」与「书写」构成的希腊语复合词。

latinIntro.en: The biblio- family through Greek and its European descendants.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 biblio- 词族及其欧洲后裔。

definition_zh: v. （为小事）争吵不休；潺潺作响
definition_en: to argue about small unimportant things; of a stream, to flow with a soft babbling sound
core_image: 两个人隔着一张餐桌，为谁该洗碗你来我往地顶嘴
scene: 两兄弟为了电视遥控器吵了一整晚。The two brothers bickered over the television remote all evening.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bicker 指为琐事持续不断地拌嘴；句意是两兄弟为电视遥控器吵了一整晚。

senses.title: To quarrel about trifles
senses.definition: to argue repeatedly about small matters that do not really matter
senses.definitionCN: 为并不重要的小事反复争吵
senses.example: The couple bickered about the route until they missed the turn.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻为路线争吵不休，结果错过了转弯。
senses.why: The word began as a name for a small skirmish, so it keeps the idea of a fight that is not a war.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指小规模交锋，因此始终带着「不是战争的打斗」之意。

senses.title: Of a stream, to babble
senses.definition: to make the light running sound of water over stones
senses.definitionCN: 水流过石头时发出的细碎声响
senses.example: A stream bickered under the wooden bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小溪在木桥下潺潺作响。
senses.why: A small stream sounds like two people trading words, so the quarrel sense was lent to water.
senses.whyCN: 小溪的声音像两个人你来我往地顶嘴，于是「争吵」义借给了流水。

intro.en: Bicker is of uncertain origin; it first names a small skirmish, then a petty quarrel, and later the sound of running water.
intro.cn: bicker 词源不确定；它先指小规模交锋，再指琐碎争吵，后来也指流水的声音。

items.en: Middle English bikeren means to attack or skirmish.
items.cn: 中古英语 bikeren 意为攻击、小规模交锋。

items.en: The earliest recorded use is a clash, not a quarrel.
items.cn: 最早记载的用法是冲突，而不是口角。

items.en: The word shifts from blows to words exchanged over trifles.
items.cn: 这个词由动手转为琐事上的你来我往。

items.en: The modern pattern of constant small quarrelling settles in.
items.cn: 「持续的小争吵」这一现代用法固定下来。

items.en: Writers borrow the word for water running over stones.
items.cn: 作家把这词借去形容水过石头的声音。

items.en: Bicker now almost always means a low-level, ongoing dispute.
items.cn: 现代 bicker 几乎总指低烈度、持续不断的争执。

note.en: The look-alike group rhymes with bicker; the near-meaning group arranges the words from a running low quarrel to a formal dispute.
note.cn: 形近组与 bicker 押韵；近义组由低烈度的持续口角排到正式的争辩。

entries.definition: To shine with an unsteady light.
To laugh in a suppressed, mocking way.
A device that makes a regular ticking sound.
A person or thing that kicks.
To quarrel noisily about something trivial.
To argue at length and crossly.
To give reasons for and against something.

normalIntro.en: Bicker sounds like two chickens pecking at each other over a grain of corn.
normalIntro.cn: bicker 听起来像两只鸡为一粒玉米互相啄来啄去。

normal.en: Say bicker quickly and you hear a small, repeated snap.
normal.cn: 快念 bicker，能听见细碎而不断的一下一下。

normal.en: It began as a skirmish, a fight too small to call a battle.
normal.cn: 它原指一场小到称不上战役的交锋。

normal.en: Bicker is a quarrel with no winner and no end.
normal.cn: bicker 是一场没有胜负也没有尽头的争吵。

normal.en: The same small snapping sound belongs to a stream.
normal.cn: 同样的细碎断续声也属于一条小溪。

normal.en: If nobody will remember the issue tomorrow, it is a bicker.
normal.cn: 如果明天没人记得争的是什么，那就是 bicker。

abstract.en: Two keys tapping the same small argument.
abstract.cn: 两把钥匙反复敲同一个不值一提的争论。

abstract.en: A duel fought with teaspoons.
abstract.cn: 用茶匙进行的决斗。

abstract.en: Noise that never turns into a decision.
abstract.cn: 始终无法变成决定的声音。

examples.en: They bickered about whose turn it was to pay.
examples.cn: 他们为轮到谁付钱而拌嘴。

examples.en: The neighbours bicker over the parking space every week.
examples.cn: 邻居每周都为车位争吵。

examples.en: A small brook bickered beneath the planks.
examples.cn: 一条小溪在木板桥下潺潺作响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必磕」——为一点小事一定要磕到底，谁也不让谁。

root: 中古英语 bikeren（小规模交锋），词源不确定，可能为拟声

sensesIntro.en: The quarrel sense and the water sense share one sound: a small, fast, repeated tapping that never quite stops.
sensesIntro.cn: 争吵义与流水义共有一个声音：细碎、快速、反复不停。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people leaning across a table, each holding one end of the same argument
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔桌而倾，各执同一场争论的一端

branches.en: A remote control between two hands.
branches.cn: 两只手之间的一个遥控器。

branches.en: Dishes left in the sink again.
A sound heard under a footbridge.
Small repeated noise with no conclusion.
branches.cn: 反复的小声音，没有结论。

intro.en: Bicker has an uncertain stem but takes regular English endings; the list below builds its forms and the vocabulary of quarrels.
intro.cn: bicker 词干来源不确定，但配的是规则英语词尾；下面列出它的各种形式与「争吵」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin altercari means to bandy words, iurgare to wrangle, and rixari to brawl.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 altercari 意为你来我往地争辩，iurgare 意为争吵，rixari 意为斗殴。

latinEntries.exampleCN: altercari 产生 altercation。
iurgare 是 objurgate 的来源。
rixari 产生 rixation。

definition_zh: 出价；投标；努力争取
definition_en: to offer a price, or to make an effort to get something
core_image: 拍卖师举起木槌等下一个价
scene: 拍卖师举起木槌，等着下一个价。She bid twice for the old painting.
sceneCN: 这里 bid 是「出价」（第 1 个义项：在交易中报出愿付的价钱）；句意是她为那幅旧画出了两次价。

derivatives.zh: 由 bid 加 -der 构成，义为「出价者」
由 bid 加 -ding 构成，义为「竞标」
由 out- 加 bid 构成，义为「出价高于」
由 over- 加 bid 构成，义为「出价过高」

senses.title: To offer a price
senses.definition: to offer a sum of money for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某物报出愿付的价钱
senses.example: She bid twice for the old painting.
senses.exampleCN: 她为那幅旧画出了两次价。
senses.why: This is the commercial sense, heard at auctions and tenders.
senses.whyCN: 这是商业义，常见于拍卖与招标场合。

senses.title: To say farewell
senses.definition: to say goodbye or greet someone formally
senses.definitionCN: 正式道别或问候
senses.example: He bade farewell to his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他向朋友们道别。
senses.why: The old sense was to announce or command, and farewell kept it.
senses.whyCN: 古义是「宣告、吩咐」，道别保留了这一层。

senses.title: To try to win something
senses.definition: to make an effort to gain something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而努力
senses.example: The city will bid to host the games.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市将申办运动会。
senses.why: Offering a price turned into offering a plan or effort.
senses.whyCN: 报出价钱，引申为报出方案或努力。

intro.en: Bid comes from an Old English verb meaning to offer or command.
intro.cn: bid 来自一个意为「提供、吩咐」的古英语动词。

items.en: beodan meant to offer or announce.
items.cn: beodan 意为「提供、宣告」。

items.en: bidden meant to command or ask.
items.cn: bidden 意为「吩咐、请求」。

items.en: bid named a price at an auction.
items.cn: bid 指拍卖中的出价。

items.en: bid for contracts became common.
items.cn: 投标承接合同变得常见。

items.en: the past tense stays bid.
items.cn: 如今过去式仍是 bid。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group gives offer words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是表示报价的词。

entries.definition: to say you will pay or give

normalIntro.en: Bid is the price you offer and the effort you offer.
normalIntro.cn: bid 既是你报出的价钱，也是你付出的努力。

normal.en: The past tense is bid, not bidded.
normal.cn: 过去式是 bid，不是 bidded。

normal.en: Bid for means offer money for.
normal.cn: bid for 指为……出价。

normal.en: The person is a bidder.
normal.cn: 出价的人叫 bidder。

normal.en: Outbid means offer more than others.
normal.cn: outbid 指出价高于别人。

normal.en: Bid farewell is a formal goodbye.
normal.cn: bid farewell 是正式道别。

abstract.en: See an auctioneer holding a wooden hammer.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖师握着木槌。

abstract.en: See a hand raised with a number.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起报出数字。

abstract.en: See a sealed envelope sent for a contract.
abstract.cn: 想象为合同寄出的密封信封。

examples.en: She bid twice for the old painting.
examples.cn: 她为那幅旧画出了两次价。

examples.en: He bade farewell to his friends.
examples.cn: 他向朋友们道别。

examples.en: The city will bid to host the games.
examples.cn: 这座城市将申办运动会。

dict_mnemonic.text: bid 短促有力，像拍卖场上举手喊价的一声。

root: 古英语 beodan 意为「提供、宣告」，中古英语 bidden 转为「吩咐、请求」，十六世纪起指拍卖出价，十九世纪起指投标与申办。

sensesIntro.en: Offering money, offering a farewell and offering an effort share one old verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 报出价钱、道出告别、付出努力，共用一个古老动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an auctioneer holding a wooden hammer.
core.cn: 核心意象：握着木槌的拍卖师。

intro.en: Bid doubles its d before -ing, and takes out- and over-.
intro.cn: bid 加 -ing 要双写 d，并能加 out-、over-。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古英语。

definition_zh: adj. 双边的，双方的（尤指两国之间）；两侧对称的
definition_en: involving two parties, especially two countries; affecting or arranged on both sides
core_image: 长桌两端各坐一人，同一份文件被同时推到两边
scene: 两国签署了一份双边贸易协定。The two countries signed a bilateral trade agreement.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bilateral 指涉及双方（尤指两国）的；句意是两国签署了一份双边贸易协定。

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Involving two parties or states
senses.definition: involving or agreed by two parties, especially two governments
senses.definitionCN: 由两方（尤指两国政府）参与或达成的
senses.example: The two ministers opened bilateral talks on energy.
senses.exampleCN: 两位部长启动了能源双边会谈。
senses.why: Bi- means two and latus means side, so bilateral is literally two-sided.
senses.whyCN: bi- 意为二，latus 意为边，bilateral 字面就是「两边的」。

senses.title: Affecting both sides of a body
senses.definition: affecting or occurring on both left and right sides of an organism
senses.definitionCN: 发生在生物体左右两侧的
senses.example: The scan showed bilateral damage to the lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示双肺均有损伤。
senses.why: The anatomical sense keeps the plain geometric meaning: the same thing on both sides.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学义保留最朴素的几何含义：两侧同时如此。

intro.en: Bilateral is Latin bi-, two, on latus, side, with the adjective ending -alis.
intro.cn: bilateral 是拉丁语 bi-（二）加 latus（边），再接形容词词尾 -alis。

items.en: Latus means a side or flank, and it is not related to lat- meaning wide.
items.cn: latus 意为边、侧面，与表示「宽」的 lat- 无关。

items.en: Bi- is the combining form of bis, twice.
items.cn: bi- 是 bis（两次）的构词形式。

items.en: Lateralis means belonging to the side.
items.cn: lateralis 意为属于侧面的。

items.en: Bilateral enters English as a geometry and anatomy term.
items.cn: bilateral 进入英语时是几何与解剖术语。

items.en: Treaties between exactly two states are called bilateral.
items.cn: 恰好两国间的条约被称作 bilateral。

items.en: The word now covers contracts, aid and both-side symptoms.
items.cn: 现代该词涵盖合同、援助与双侧症状。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bi- front; the near-meaning group distinguishes how many sides are actually involved.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bi- 开头；近义组分辨实际涉及几方。

entries.definition: Happening every two months or twice a month.
entries.definitionCN: 两月一次或一月两次的。

entries.definition: Having two poles or two opposite extremes.
Shared or done by each toward the other.
Given by each side to the other.

normalIntro.en: Break it into bi, two, and lateral, side: a bilateral deal is one signed from both sides of a table.
normalIntro.cn: 把它拆成 bi（二）与 lateral（侧边）：双边协定就是从桌子两边共同签下的。

normal.en: Lateral means side, as in a lateral pass.
normal.cn: lateral 意为侧边，如 lateral pass（侧传）。

normal.en: Bi- means two, as in bicycle and bilingual.
normal.cn: bi- 意为二，如 bicycle、bilingual。

normal.en: So bilateral is simply two-sided.
normal.cn: 所以 bilateral 就是「两侧的」。

normal.en: Two governments at one table make a bilateral treaty.
normal.cn: 两国政府同坐一桌，就有了双边条约。

normal.en: Two lungs damaged at once is also bilateral.
normal.cn: 双肺同时受损也叫 bilateral。

abstract.en: One document with two signatures.
abstract.cn: 一份文件，两个签名。

abstract.en: A handshake written into law.
abstract.cn: 写进法律的一次握手。

abstract.en: Symmetry across the line of a table.
abstract.cn: 跨过桌面中线的对称。

examples.en: Both sides described the bilateral meeting as productive.
examples.cn: 双方都称这次双边会晤富有成效。

examples.en: The disease causes bilateral hearing loss.
examples.cn: 这种病会造成双侧听力损失。

examples.en: Aid was agreed on a bilateral basis rather than through the union.
examples.cn: 援助是由双边商定的，而不是通过联盟。

dict_mnemonic.text: bi 是「二」，lateral 是「侧边」——两个人从桌子两侧同时伸手，这就是双边。

root: 拉丁 bi-（二）+ latus / later-（边、侧）+ -al（形容词后缀）

sensesIntro.en: The political sense and the medical sense are the same geometry: one thing happening on two sides.
sensesIntro.cn: 政治义与医学义是同一个几何：同一件事在两侧同时发生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one paper pushed from both ends of a long table at the same moment
core.cn: 核心意象：同一份文件在长桌两端被同时推出

branches.en: Two lungs showing the same shadow.
Two ears tested one after the other.

intro.en: Bilateral is built from a numeric prefix and a Latin side; the list below separates the pieces and their relatives.
intro.cn: bilateral 由一个数字前缀与一个拉丁语「边」构成；下面把各部件及其亲属分开排列。

latinIntro.en: Latin latus is a side, bis is twice, and lateralis means of the side.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 latus 意为边，bis 意为两次，lateralis 意为侧面的。

latinEntries.exampleCN: latus 产生 lateral 与 bilateral。
bis 变成前缀 bi-。
lateralis 产生英语 lateral。

definition_zh: 双语的；使用两种语言的；双语并用的（也可作名词：双语者）
definition_en: using or written in two languages, or able to speak two languages
core_image: 一张对开的告示纸，左半边与右半边写着同样内容却用两种文字，中间用一条细线分开
scene: 社区公告栏上贴着一张对开的告示，左右两半内容相同，文字却不同。Every bilingual form in the office carried the same sentence twice.
sceneCN: 这里指「同时使用两种语言的」（第 1 个义项：涉及两种语言并用）；句意为办公室里的每份双语表格都把同一句话写了两遍。可辨识物件：告示、对开纸、两种文字、公告栏。

pos.zh: 双语的；使用两种语言的

senses.title: Using two languages
senses.definition: describing a thing, service or activity that works in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述以两种语言运作的事物、服务或活动
senses.example: The bilingual help desk answers in Mandarin and English.
senses.exampleCN: 双语服务台用普通话与英语应答。
senses.why: the word pairs a prefix for 'two' with the Latin word for tongue, so it counts two languages exactly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表「二」的前缀与拉丁语表「舌头」的词相连，精确地数两种语言。

senses.title: A person who speaks two languages
senses.definition: describing someone who can use two languages in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 描述能在日常生活中使用两种语言的人
senses.example: She grew up bilingual and still dreams in both.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小双语成长，至今仍用两种语言做梦。
senses.why: a person who carries the pair through a whole life is the human face of the count.
senses.whyCN: 把这一对语言带过一生的人，是这个数目的「人面」。

senses.title: A text or sign in two languages
senses.titleCN: 用两种语言写成的文本或标牌
senses.definition: printed or displayed in two languages at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时以两种语言印刷或展示
senses.example: The bilingual label lists every ingredient twice.
senses.exampleCN: 双语标签把每种成分列出两遍。
senses.why: two languages printed side by side make the pair visible.
senses.whyCN: 两种语言并排印出，就让这一对变得可见。

senses.title: Bilingual education
senses.definition: schooling in which two languages serve as media of instruction
senses.definitionCN: 以两种语言作为教学语言的教育
senses.example: Bilingual education delayed the shift to the majority language.
senses.exampleCN: 双语教育推迟了向多数语言的转换。
senses.why: a school that teaches in two languages turns the count into a curriculum.
senses.whyCN: 用两种语言教学的学校，把这个数目变成课程。

senses.title: A bilingual community or region
senses.definition: describing a place where two languages are in everyday use
senses.definitionCN: 描述两种语言在日常中并用的地方
senses.example: The valley has been bilingual since the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路开通以来，这条山谷一直双语并存。
senses.why: a whole place can hold the pair for generations, so the adjective describes geography as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 整个地方能把这一对保留几代，因此这个形容词既描述人也描述地理。

senses.title: Bilingual processing in the mind
senses.definition: describing research on how one mind stores and switches between two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述对同一心智如何储存并切换两种语言的研究
senses.example: Bilingual speakers separate their languages by context, not by effort.
senses.exampleCN: 双语说话者按场合区分语言，而不是靠费力控制。
senses.why: a mind that holds two systems is the pair studied from inside.
senses.whyCN: 容纳两套系统的心智，是从内部研究的「这一对」。

senses.title: A bilingual dictionary or resource
senses.definition: a reference that gives equivalents in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 给出两种语言对应说法的工具书
senses.example: The bilingual dictionary marks which word fits which register.
senses.exampleCN: 这本双语词典标出哪个词属哪种语域。
senses.why: a dictionary exists to place one language beside the other.
senses.whyCN: 词典的存在，就是把一种语言放在另一种旁边。

senses.title: Bilingual policy or rights
senses.definition: describing official arrangements that guarantee services in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述保障以两种语言提供服务的官方安排
senses.example: Bilingual policy made every statute readable in both tongues.
senses.exampleCN: 双语政策使每项法规都能以两种语言阅读。
senses.why: a promise made in law must appear in both tongues, which turns the count into an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法律作出的承诺必须以两种语言出现，这就把数目变成义务。

intro.en: Bilingual comes from Latin bilinguis 'two-tongued', built on bis 'twice' and lingua 'tongue, language'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 bilinguis「双舌的」，由表「两次」的成分与 lingua「舌头、语言」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and, by extension, 'language'. Its deeper origin is unsettled and no older attested form is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 指「舌头」，引申为「语言」。其更深来源无定论，也没有公认的更早书证形式。

items.en: Bilinguis meant 'two-tongued'. In Roman usage it could also mean 'double-tongued', that is, deceitful, a sense that English did not keep.
items.cn: bilinguis 意为「双舌的」。在罗马用法中它也可指「两面三刀的」，即欺骗性的，这一含义英语没有保留。

items.en: English formed the modern adjective in the nineteenth century, when schooling and censuses made two-language populations visible.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪形成这个现代形容词，当时学校教育与人口普查使双语人群变得可见。

items.en: The twentieth century gave the word a policy life, naming programs that teach in two languages.
items.cn: 二十世纪赋予这个词政策生命，用来指以两种语言教学的项目。

items.en: Psychology and neuroscience later used it for the mental organisation of two language systems.
items.cn: 心理学与神经科学后来用它指两套语言系统在心智中的组织方式。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root is unknown, and the first English use of the modern sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语之前的词根不明，这个现代义在英语中最早使用的年代只能约略推定。

note.en: Group one holds the counting words that are constantly confused; group two holds terms about two-language arrangements.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的计数词；第二组是关于两种语言安排的术语。

entries.definition: Using several languages, often without a fixed count; bilingual is the exact two.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用多种语言，常不限定数目；双语则精确指两种。

entries.definition: Using a single language; it is the opposite pole of the same counting series.
entries.definitionCN: 指只使用一种语言，是同一计数序列的另一端。

entries.definition: The state or practice of having two languages; the adjective describes what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有两种语言的状态或实践；形容词则描述名词所指的情形。

entries.definition: A rare word for a person who speaks two languages; bilingual is far commoner as the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说两种语言者的罕用名词；双语一词作名词更常见。

entries.definition: A common label for two-language school programs; it is a compound rather than a Latin borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 指双语学校项目的常见标签，属复合词而非拉丁借词。

entries.definition: A literal English rendering of the Latin word; in older use it could also mean deceitful.
entries.definitionCN: 是那个拉丁词的直译英语说法；旧用法中也可指欺骗性的。

entries.definition: Using two dialects of one language, a narrower case than two separate languages.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用同一种语言的两种方言，范围比两种独立语言更窄。

entries.definition: The act of moving between languages in conversation; bilingual describes the capacity behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指会话中在语言间切换的行为；双语描述其背后的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means two and the root means tongue, so the word literally has two tongues.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「二」，词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词字面上就是「有两条舌头」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach it to services: bilingual signs, forms, help desk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它挂到服务上：双语标识、双语表格、双语服务台。

normal.en: It sits exactly in the middle of the counting ladder: one, two, many.
normal.cn: 它正好在计数阶梯的中间：单语、双语、多语。

normal.en: The family runs bilingualism, bilingually, bilinguals, multilingual, monolingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「双语现象」「以双语方式」「双语者」「多语的」「单语的」。

normal.en: A split notice with the same sentence twice is the picture to hold.
normal.cn: 一张左右分栏、同一句话写两遍的告示，是要留住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture two doors side by side, both opening into the same room.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两道门，都通向同一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a mind with two indexes to the same world.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头脑，为同一个世界备有两套索引。

abstract.en: Picture a single sentence walking across a thin line and changing its clothes.
abstract.cn: 想象同一句话跨过一条细线，换了一身衣服。

examples.en: Bilingual ballots were introduced after the court ruling.
examples.cn: 法院裁决之后，双语选票开始启用。

examples.en: Children in bilingual programs read in both languages by nine.
examples.cn: 参加双语项目的孩子到九岁已能用两种语言阅读。

examples.en: The bilingual dictionary distinguishes formal from everyday words.
examples.cn: 这本双语词典区分正式词与日常词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拜林圭尔」——拜两条舌头所赐，两种话都能说，这就是双语的。

root: 拉丁 bilinguis「双舌的」由表「两次」的成分与 lingua「舌头、语言」构成；罗马用法中亦可指「两面三刀的」，该贬义未被英语保留。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses pair two languages across a person, a sign, a school, a valley, a mind, a dictionary and a law.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把两种语言配到人、标牌、学校、山谷、心智、词典与法律之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sheet folded down the middle, the same sentence on both halves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从中间对折的纸，两半写着同一句话。

branches.en: THE COUNT: exactly two languages is the word's whole definition.
branches.cn: 数目：正好两种语言，就是这个词的全部定义。

branches.en: THE SPEAKER: a person can carry both languages through a whole life.
branches.cn: 说话者：一个人可以把两种语言带过一生。

branches.en: WORDS ON PAPER: labels and dictionaries put the two side by side.
branches.cn: 纸上的词：标签与词典把两者并排放置。

branches.en: PLACES THAT TEACH: schools and whole valleys keep two languages alive together.
branches.cn: 教学之地：学校与整条山谷让两种语言一同存活。

branches.en: MIND AND LAW: one brain holds both, and one statute can promise both.
branches.cn: 心智与法律：一个头脑容纳两者，一项法规也能承诺两者。

intro.en: The word is two Latin pieces and an English adjective ending, and each piece also builds a family.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个拉丁成分与一个英语形容词词尾构成，每个成分也都构成一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis 'twice' supplies the counting prefix, Latin lingua the root, and the adjective ending makes the description; the same pieces build multilingual and monolingual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bis「两次」提供计数前缀，拉丁 lingua 提供词根，形容词词尾完成描述；同样的成分也构成「多语的」与「单语的」。

items.example: The prefix fixes the count at exactly two.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把数目固定为二。

items.example: The root names what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被计数的东西。

items.example: The ending turns the count into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把数目变成描述。

items.example: The bilingual form served both communities.
items.exampleCN: 这份双语表格服务两个社群。

items.example: Bilingualism began at home, not at school.
items.exampleCN: 双语现象始于家庭，而非学校。

items.example: A multilingual city outgrows the pair.
items.exampleCN: 一座多语城市超出了「两种」的范围。

definition_zh: n. 双语能力；双语现象；（国家的）双语制度
definition_en: the ability to use two languages; the practice of using two languages in a country or a school
core_image: 一个人在同一天里，上午用母语开会，下午用另一种语言点咖啡
scene: 在双语家庭长大的孩子自然而然地拥有双语能力。Children raised in a bilingual household develop bilingualism naturally.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bilingualism 指使用两种语言的能力；句意是在双语家庭长大的孩子自然具备双语能力。

forms.label: 不可数名词（一般无复数）

senses.title: The ability to use two languages
senses.definition: the state of being able to speak and understand two languages
senses.definitionCN: 能够说并理解两种语言的状态
senses.example: Her bilingualism opened doors in two job markets.
senses.exampleCN: 她的双语能力为她打开了两边的就业市场。
senses.why: The suffix -ism turns the adjective bilingual into the name of a condition or ability.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 把形容词 bilingual 变成一种状态或能力的名称。

senses.title: A policy of two official languages
senses.definition: an official arrangement in which two languages are used in public life
senses.definitionCN: 公共生活中同时使用两种语言的正式安排
senses.example: Official bilingualism shapes every sign in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 官方双语制度决定了首都每一块标牌的写法。
senses.why: The same noun names both what a person has and what a state practises.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指个人拥有的能力，也指国家实行的制度。

intro.en: Bilingualism is Latin bi-, two, plus lingua, tongue, plus the noun ending -ismus.
intro.cn: bilingualism 是拉丁语 bi-（二）加 lingua（舌头、语言），再加名词词尾 -ismus。

items.en: Lingua means tongue and, by extension, a language.
items.cn: lingua 意为舌头，引申为语言。

items.en: Bilinguis describes someone with two tongues.
items.cn: bilinguis 形容「有两条舌头」的人。

items.en: English bilingual names a person or text in two languages.
items.cn: 英语 bilingual 指使用两种语言的人或双语文本。

items.en: The -ism noun names the condition rather than the person.
items.cn: 加 -ism 的名词指状态，而不是人。

items.en: Schools adopt the word for teaching through two languages.
items.cn: 学校用这个词指用两种语言授课。

items.en: Official bilingualism becomes a term of law and politics.
items.cn: 官方双语成为法律与政治术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bi- or -ism shape; the near-meaning group counts how many languages are in play.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bi- 或 -ism 的形状；近义组按涉及的语言数量排列。

entries.definition: A sound made with both lips.
Every two months or twice a month.
entries.definitionCN: 两月一次或一月两次的。

entries.definition: The use of a single language.
Two varieties of one language used for different purposes.
entries.definitionCN: 同一语言的两种变体分工使用。

normalIntro.en: Lingua is tongue, so bilingualism is literally having two tongues at your service.
normalIntro.cn: lingua 是舌头，所以 bilingualism 字面就是「有两条舌头可用」。

normal.en: Lingua means tongue, as in linguistics and language.
normal.cn: lingua 意为舌头，如 linguistics 与 language。

normal.en: Bi- adds two, so bilingual means two tongues.
normal.cn: bi- 加上二，bilingual 就是两条舌头。

normal.en: -ism turns the ability into a name.
normal.cn: -ism 把这种能力变成一个名称。

normal.en: One person, two languages, a whole working day.
normal.cn: 一个人，两种语言，一整天的工作。

normal.en: One country, two official tongues, and the word still fits.
normal.cn: 一个国家，两种官方语言，这个词同样适用。

abstract.en: Two doors into the same room.
abstract.cn: 通往同一个房间的两扇门。

abstract.en: Two dictionaries living in one head.
abstract.cn: 住在同一个脑袋里的两本词典。

abstract.en: A tongue that changes coat by the hour.
abstract.cn: 每小时换一件外衣的舌头。

examples.en: Research links bilingualism with better attention control.
examples.cn: 研究把双语能力与更好的注意力控制联系起来。

examples.en: Official bilingualism requires every form in two languages.
examples.cn: 官方双语制度要求每张表格都有两种语言版本。

examples.en: Her bilingualism came from a childhood split between two cities.
examples.cn: 她的双语能力来自在两个城市之间度过的童年。

dict_mnemonic.text: bi 是「二」，lingua 是「舌头」，-ism 是「状态」——一个人身上装着两条舌头，就是双语能力。

root: 拉丁 bi-（二）+ lingua（舌头、语言）+ -ism（状态、制度）

sensesIntro.en: The noun has two faces: a skill inside one head, and a rule inside one state.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词有两副面孔：一个人头脑里的技能，以及一个国家里的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one speaker moving all day between two languages without noticing the switch
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个人整天在两种语言间来回，却察觉不到切换

branches.en: A morning meeting in one tongue.
Coffee ordered in the other by noon.
branches.cn: 中午用另一种语言点的咖啡。
备着两支麦克风的议会。

branches.en: Two languages held as ordinary equipment.
branches.cn: 把两种语言当作日常装备。

intro.en: Bilingualism is a numeric prefix, a Latin tongue, and a noun ending; the list below builds the whole family of language-count words.
intro.cn: bilingualism 由数字前缀、拉丁语「舌头」和名词词尾构成；下面列出整族「数语言」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua is tongue, bilinguis is two-tongued, and loqui is to speak.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 意为舌头，bilinguis 意为双舌的，loqui 意为说话。

latinEntries.exampleCN: lingua 产生 language 与 linguistics。
bilinguis 产生 bilingual。
loqui 产生 loquacious 与 eloquent。

definition_zh: 账单；法案；鸟喙
definition_en: a statement of money owed, a proposed law, or a bird's beak
core_image: 餐馆桌角压着的那张长条账单
scene: 账单压在餐馆桌角，旁边放着找零。He paid the bill and left a tip.
sceneCN: 这里 bill 是「账单」（第 1 个义项：列出应付金额的单据）；句意是他付了账单并留下小费。

derivatives.zh: 由 bill 加 -ing 构成，义为「开票、计费」
由 bill 与 board 复合，义为「广告牌」

senses.title: A statement of money owed
senses.definition: a paper listing money that must be paid
senses.definitionCN: 列出应付金额的单据
senses.example: He paid the bill and left a tip.
senses.exampleCN: 他付了账单并留下小费。
senses.why: This comes from a word for a sealed document.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自表示「盖印文书」的词。

senses.title: A proposed law
senses.definition: a draft law put before a parliament
senses.definitionCN: 提交议会审议的法律草案
senses.example: The bill passed after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长时间辩论，法案通过了。
senses.why: A bill was once a royal document, so laws kept the name.
senses.whyCN: bill 曾是皇家文书，法律沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: A bird's beak
senses.definition: the hard mouth of a bird
senses.definitionCN: 鸟类坚硬的嘴
senses.example: The bird cleaned its bill on the branch.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟在树枝上擦拭喙。
senses.why: This sense has a separate Old English root, bile.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项另有古英语词根 bile。

intro.en: Bill joins two histories: a Latin document and an Old English beak.
intro.cn: bill 汇合了两条历史：拉丁语的文书与古英语的鸟喙。

items.en: bulla meant a sealed document.
items.cn: bulla 意为「盖印文书」。

items.en: billa named a written list.
items.cn: billa 指书面清单。

items.en: bill meant a note of money owed.
items.cn: bill 指欠款单据。

items.en: parliament used bill for a draft law.
items.cn: 议会用 bill 指法律草案。

items.en: bile meant a bird's beak.
items.cn: 古英语 bile 指鸟喙。

items.en: both senses live on in one spelling.
items.cn: 两个义项在同一个拼写里并存。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group gives payment words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是付款相关词。

entries.definition: a list of goods and money due

normalIntro.en: Bill is paper that asks for money, paper that proposes law, and a bird's hard mouth.
normalIntro.cn: bill 既是要钱的纸、提议法律的纸，也是鸟的硬嘴。

normal.en: The plural is bills.
normal.cn: 复数是 bills。

normal.en: Pay the bill at the counter.
normal.cn: 到柜台付账。

normal.en: A bill can also be a draft law.
normal.cn: bill 也可以指法律草案。

normal.en: A bird's bill is its beak.
normal.cn: 鸟的 bill 就是喙。

normal.en: Billed means charged or advertised.
normal.cn: billed 指被收费或被宣传。

abstract.en: See a long paper slip under a cup.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子下压着的长条单据。

abstract.en: See hands raised to vote on a law.
abstract.cn: 想象举手对法律表决。

abstract.en: See a sparrow wiping its beak.
abstract.cn: 想象麻雀擦拭它的喙。

examples.en: He paid the bill and left a tip.
examples.cn: 他付了账单并留下小费。

examples.en: The bill passed after a long debate.
examples.cn: 经过长时间辩论，法案通过了。

examples.en: The bird cleaned its bill on the branch.
examples.cn: 鸟在树枝上擦拭喙。

dict_mnemonic.text: bill 像一张窄长的纸条，正是一张账单的形状。

root: 表示账单与法案的 bill 源自拉丁语 bulla（盖印文书），经中世纪拉丁语 billa 进入英语；表示鸟喙的 bill 则来自古英语 bile，两条来源合流为同一拼写。

sensesIntro.en: One spelling carries a debt note, a draft law and a bird's mouth.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个拼写承载欠款单、法律草案与鸟嘴三个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long paper slip under a cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子下压着的长条单据。

intro.en: Bill takes -s, -ed and -ing, and joins board to form billboard.
intro.cn: bill 可加 -s、-ed、-ing，还能与 board 复合成 billboard。

latinIntro.en: The document sense comes from Latin bulla; the beak sense is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 文书义来自拉丁语 bulla，鸟喙义来自古英语。

definition_zh: adj./adv. 两月一次的（地）；每月两次的（地）；n. 双月刊
definition_en: happening every two months, or twice a month; a publication issued on such a schedule
core_image: 日历上两个月才被圈中一格的约会，和一个月里被圈中两格的约会
scene: 这本杂志是双月刊，每两个月出一期。The magazine is bimonthly, so a new issue appears every two months.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bimonthly 可指每两个月一次的；句意是这本杂志为双月刊，两个月出一期。

pos.zh: 两月一次的；一月两次的

forms.label: 形容词与副词原级（无屈折变化）

derivatives.zh: 两周一次的；一周两次的

senses.title: Every two months
senses.definition: appearing or happening once every two months
senses.definitionCN: 每两个月出现或发生一次
senses.example: The journal is bimonthly, with six issues a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这份期刊是双月刊，一年六期。
senses.why: Bi- can be read as every, and month supplies the interval, so the word can mean once in two months.
senses.whyCN: bi- 可理解为「每隔」，加 month 表间隔，故可指两个月一次。

senses.title: Twice a month
senses.definition: appearing or happening two times in each month
senses.definitionCN: 每月出现或发生两次
senses.example: Some clinics hold bimonthly checks, one at the start and one mid-month.
senses.exampleCN: 有些诊所每月查两次，月初一次、月中一次。
senses.why: The same prefix also carries the sense of twice, so the word is famously ambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 同一个前缀也含「两次」之义，因此这个词以歧义著称。

intro.en: Bimonthly is Latin bi- joined to the English word month and the ending -ly.
intro.cn: bimonthly 是拉丁语 bi- 接英语 month，再加词尾 -ly。

items.en: Bis means twice, and its combining form is bi-.
items.cn: bis 意为两次，其构词形式为 bi-。

items.en: Old English monath is the month, named for the moon.
items.cn: 古英语 monath 即月份，因月亮而得名。

items.en: The compound bimonth appears in periodical writing.
items.cn: 复合词 bimonth 出现在期刊文字中。

items.en: Bimonthly is coined for publications and meetings.
items.cn: bimonthly 为出版物与会议而造。

items.en: Editors complain that readers cannot tell which sense is meant.
items.cn: 编辑抱怨读者分不清是哪一种含义。

items.en: Many style guides advise every two months in plain phrasing.
items.cn: 现代写作指南建议直接写成「每两个月」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bi- or -ly shape; the near-meaning group runs through the schedule words from twice a month to once a year.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bi- 或 -ly 的形状；近义组按频率从每月两次排到每年一次。

entries.definition: Every two weeks or twice a week.
entries.definitionCN: 两周一次或一周两次的。

normalIntro.en: Bi- is the ambiguous piece: it can mean twice or every two, so bimonthly covers both schedules.
normalIntro.cn: bi- 是那个含糊的部分：既可指「两次」，也可指「每隔两个」，所以 bimonthly 两种日程都管。

normal.en: Bi- plus month plus -ly, three pieces only.
normal.cn: bi- 加 month 加 -ly，只有三块。

normal.en: With two months, it is six issues a year.
normal.cn: 按两个月算，一年六期。

normal.en: With twice a month, it is twenty-four issues a year.
normal.cn: 按每月两次算，一年二十四期。

normal.en: When in doubt, spell the schedule out in words.
normal.cn: 拿不准时，干脆用文字把频率写清楚。

normal.en: Compare biannual, which has the same double reading.
normal.cn: 可比 biannual，它同样有两种读法。

abstract.en: A calendar with only two circles on it.
abstract.cn: 日历上只画了两个圈。

abstract.en: A clock with a missing hand.
abstract.cn: 缺了一根指针的钟。

abstract.en: A word that refuses to give one date.
abstract.cn: 一个不肯给出单一日期的词。

examples.en: The board meets bimonthly, in March, May and so on.
examples.cn: 董事会每两个月开一次会，三月、五月依此类推。

examples.en: Her column appears bimonthly in a science magazine.
examples.cn: 她的专栏在一份科学杂志上每两月刊出一次。

examples.en: Ask the clinic whether bimonthly here means twice a month.
examples.cn: 问问诊所这里的 bimonthly 是不是指每月两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: bi 是「二」，month 是「月」——两个月一次，也可能是一个月两次，所以看到这个词一定要问清楚。

root: 拉丁 bi-（二；每两）+ 古英语 monath（月）+ -ly（形容词、副词词尾）

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are not an accident but the prefix itself: bi- can count occurrences or count the interval.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项并非偶然，而是前缀本身：bi- 既可数次数，也可数间隔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one calendar with two circles far apart and another with two circles close together
core.cn: 核心意象：一张日历上两个相隔很远的圈，另一张上两个挨得很近的圈

branches.en: An issue arriving in spring and then in summer.
branches.cn: 春季来一期，夏季再来一期。

branches.en: A review meeting every other month.
A check on the first and the fifteenth.
branches.cn: 一日与十五日各查一次。
一个月里的两个发薪日。

branches.en: A frequency that must be asked about.

intro.en: Bimonthly stacks a Latin numeral, an English time word and a suffix; the list below builds the whole family of frequency words.
intro.cn: bimonthly 由一个拉丁数词、一个英语时间词和一个词尾叠成；下面列出整族频率词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis is twice, mensis is a month, and annus is a year.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bis 意为两次，mensis 意为月，annus 意为年。

items.exampleCN: 每月两次的；半年一次的

latinEntries.exampleCN: bis 变成前缀 bi-。

latinEntries.example: Mensis lies behind menstrual and semester.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mensis 是 menstrual 与 semester 的来源。
annus 产生 annual 与 anniversary。

definition_zh: 箱；垃圾桶
definition_en: a container for storing things or for waste
core_image: 厨房角落装着菜叶的桶
scene: 厨房角落的桶里堆着菜叶。He threw the peel into the bin.
sceneCN: 这里 bin 是「垃圾桶」（第 2 个义项：盛放废弃物的容器）；句意是他把果皮扔进了垃圾桶。

pos.zh: 动词：把……扔进垃圾桶；丢弃

derivatives.zh: 由 bin 与 man 复合，英式英语指「垃圾清运工」
由 dust 与 bin 复合，英式英语指「垃圾桶」

senses.title: A storage container
senses.definition: a container for keeping things in
senses.definitionCN: 用来存放物品的容器
senses.example: Store the rice in a dry bin.
senses.exampleCN: 把米存放在干燥的箱子里。
senses.why: This is the older sense, a simple basket or box.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的义项，指简单的筐或箱。

senses.title: A waste container
senses.definition: a container for things thrown away
senses.definitionCN: 盛放废弃物的容器
senses.example: He threw the peel into the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把果皮扔进了垃圾桶。
senses.why: The same container became the place for rubbish at home.
senses.whyCN: 同一种容器在家里成了丢废弃物的地方。

senses.title: To throw something away
senses.definition: to put something in the bin
senses.definitionCN: 把某物扔进垃圾桶
senses.example: They binned the old papers.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把旧文件丢了。
senses.why: The container became a verb for the act of discarding.
senses.whyCN: 容器转为动词，表示丢弃的动作。

intro.en: Bin is an Old English word for a basket, probably from Latin.
intro.cn: bin 是古英语中表示筐的词，可能源自拉丁语。

items.en: binne meant a basket or crib.
items.cn: binne 意为「筐、储物格」。

items.en: bins held grain and coal.
items.cn: 箱筐用来装谷物和煤。

items.en: bin named a household rubbish container.
items.cn: bin 指家庭垃圾桶。

items.en: recycling bins appeared in cities.
items.cn: 回收箱出现在城市里。

items.en: bin also works as a verb.
items.cn: 如今 bin 也作动词使用。
