note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是各类容器。

entries.definition: a container made of woven material

normalIntro.en: A bin holds things, and later holds what we throw away.
normalIntro.cn: bin 先用来装东西，后来装我们丢掉的东西。

normal.en: The plural is bins.
normal.cn: 复数是 bins。

normal.en: A rubbish bin is for waste.
normal.cn: rubbish bin 用来装垃圾。

normal.en: A bin liner keeps the bin clean.
normal.cn: bin liner 让桶保持干净。

normal.en: The verb binned means threw away.
normal.cn: 动词 binned 指丢掉了。

normal.en: British English prefers bin to trash can.
normal.cn: 英式英语更常说 bin。

abstract.en: See vegetable peel piled in a kitchen bin.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房桶里堆着菜叶。

abstract.en: See three coloured bins by a gate.
abstract.cn: 想象门口三只不同颜色的桶。

abstract.en: See a hand dropping paper into a bin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把纸丢进桶里。

examples.en: He threw the peel into the bin.
examples.cn: 他把果皮扔进了垃圾桶。

examples.en: Store the rice in a dry bin.
examples.cn: 把米存放在干燥的箱子里。

examples.en: They binned the old papers.
examples.cn: 他们把旧文件丢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: bin 的 b 与 n 像桶的两道壁，中间装东西。

root: 古英语 binne 指筐或储物格，可能借自拉丁语；中古英语用来装谷物与煤，十九世纪起指家庭垃圾桶，二十世纪出现分类回收箱，并发展出动词用法。

sensesIntro.en: The same container stores grain and receives rubbish.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种容器，既存放谷物，也接收垃圾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vegetable peel piled in a kitchen bin.
core.cn: 核心意象：厨房桶里堆着菜叶。

intro.en: Bin doubles its n before -ed and -ing, and joins man and dust.
intro.cn: bin 加 -ed、-ing 要双写 n，并能与 man、dust 复合。

latinIntro.en: The word is Old English, possibly from Latin benna.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自古英语，可能源自拉丁语 benna。

definition_zh: 捆绑；装订；约束
definition_en: to tie things together, or to place an obligation on someone
core_image: 麻绳把一摞纸箱牢牢捆住
scene: 麻绳把纸箱牢牢捆在一起。They bound the boxes with rope.
sceneCN: 这里 bind 是「捆绑」（第 1 个义项：用绳带把东西系在一起）；句意是他们用绳子把箱子捆好。

derivatives.zh: 由 bind 加 -ing 构成，义为「有约束力的」
由 bind 加 -er 构成，义为「装订工、活页夹」
由 un- 加 bind 构成，义为「解开」

senses.title: To tie together
senses.definition: to tie things together with rope or string
senses.definitionCN: 用绳或带把东西系在一起
senses.example: They bound the boxes with rope.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用绳子把箱子捆好。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, working with hands and rope.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，用双手与绳索完成。

senses.title: To fasten pages into a book
senses.definition: to fasten pages together as a book
senses.definitionCN: 把书页固定成册
senses.example: The pages were bound in leather.
senses.exampleCN: 书页被装订上皮面。
senses.why: Binding a book is tying pages the way rope ties boxes.
senses.whyCN: 装订书就是像捆箱子那样把书页系住。

senses.title: To place an obligation
senses.definition: to place a legal or moral duty on someone
senses.definitionCN: 给某人加上法律或道义上的义务
senses.example: The contract binds both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这份合同对双方都有约束力。
senses.why: A promise ties a person the way rope ties a load.
senses.whyCN: 承诺把人系住，就像绳子系住货物。

intro.en: Bind is an ancient Germanic verb for tying.
intro.cn: bind 是日耳曼语中表示「系、捆」的古老动词。

items.en: bindan meant to tie.
items.cn: bindan 意为「捆绑」。

items.en: bind also meant to make a book.
items.cn: bind 也开始表示「装订」。

items.en: the word described legal duty.

items.cn: bound 成为过去式。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives tying words.

entries.definition: to join one thing to another

normalIntro.en: Bind ties rope, pages and promises alike.
normalIntro.cn: bind 把绳索、书页与承诺一样系住。

normal.en: The past tense is bound.
normal.cn: 过去式是 bound。

normal.en: Binding means having legal force.
normal.cn: binding 指具有法律效力。

normal.en: A binder holds loose pages.
normal.cn: binder 是装活页的夹子。

normal.en: Bind up a wound means wrap it.
normal.cn: bind up a wound 指包扎伤口。

normal.en: Unbind means to set free.
normal.cn: unbind 指解开、释放。

abstract.en: See rope pulled tight around boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象绳子紧勒住纸箱。

abstract.en: See hands pressing pages into a cover.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把书页压进封皮。

abstract.en: See a signed contract on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上签好的合同。

examples.en: They bound the boxes with rope.

examples.en: The pages were bound in leather.
examples.cn: 书页被装订上皮面。

examples.en: The contract binds both sides.
examples.cn: 这份合同对双方都有约束力。

dict_mnemonic.text: b 与 d 像两根柱子，中间用绳捆住，就是 bind。

root: 古英语 bindan 意为捆绑，中古英语起用于装订书籍，十四世纪引申出法律与道义上的约束，过去式 bound 沿用至今。

sensesIntro.en: Rope, bookbinding and contracts all bind in the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 绳索、装订与合同，都用同一种方式「系住」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rope pulled tight around boxes.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳子紧勒住纸箱。

intro.en: Bind takes -s and -ing, with bound as its past form.
intro.cn: bind 可加 -s、-ing，过去式是不规则的 bound。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: n. 双筒望远镜（常用复数形式）
definition_en: a pair of short telescopes joined together, held to both eyes to view distant things
core_image: 双手举着两只并排的镜筒，远处的船一下子被拉到眼前
scene: 他举起双筒望远镜，观察对岸的鸟。He raised the binoculars to watch the birds on the far shore.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：binoculars 指双手举起的双筒望远镜；句意是他举起望远镜观察对岸的鸟。

forms.label: 固定复数形式（作单件器具）

senses.title: A two-tube viewing instrument
senses.definition: an optical instrument with two parallel tubes, held to both eyes to magnify distant objects
senses.definitionCN: 两管并排、贴双眼观看以放大远处物体的光学器具
senses.example: From the ridge she could follow the whole valley with binoculars.
senses.exampleCN: 从山脊上，她用望远镜能把整条山谷看得清楚。
senses.why: Binocular comes from Latin bini, two at a time, and oculus, eye: an instrument for two eyes.
senses.whyCN: binocular 源自拉丁语 bini（成双）与 oculus（眼）：供双眼使用的器具。

senses.title: A small pair for indoor use
senses.definition: a compact pair with low magnification, used at theatres and concerts
senses.definitionCN: 低倍率、在剧院与音乐会使用的小型双筒镜
senses.example: He kept opera binoculars in his coat for the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 他在外套里放着一副观剧小望远镜，留着第二幕用。
senses.why: The same design is scaled down until it fits a pocket, and the purpose changes with the size.
senses.whyCN: 同样的构造缩小到能放进衣袋，用途便随尺寸改变。

intro.en: Binoculars joins Latin bini, two at a time, to oculus, eye.
intro.cn: binoculars 把拉丁语 bini（成双）与 oculus（眼）连在一起。

items.en: Oculus means eye and stands behind ocular and binocular.
items.cn: oculus 意为眼睛，是 ocular 与 binocular 的词根。

items.en: Bini means two at a time, the distributive form of two.
items.cn: bini 意为「每次两个」，是「二」的分配数词。

items.en: Binoculus describes something with two eyes.
items.cn: binoculus 形容有两只眼睛的东西。

items.cn: 英语 binocular 先作形容词出现。

items.en: Two-tube field glasses become standard for soldiers and sailors.
items.cn: 双筒野外镜成为士兵与水手的标准装备。

items.en: The plural noun settles as the everyday name.

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ocular build; the near-meaning group runs from the plain instrument to the words for specialised viewing devices.

entries.definition: An instrument that magnifies distant objects.

entries.definitionCN: 单手可持的小型望远镜。

normalIntro.cn: bini 意为成双，oculus 意为眼，binoculars 就是两只玻璃做的眼睛。

normal.en: Two glass eyes held up bring the horizon close.

abstract.en: Borrowed eyes on a strap.

abstract.en: Distance folded into two circles.
abstract.cn: 把距离折进两个圆里。

abstract.en: Attention made into an instrument.

examples.en: She scanned the ridge line with her binoculars.

examples.en: These binoculars are waterproof and filled with nitrogen.
examples.cn: 这副望远镜防水，内充氮气。

examples.en: He forgot the binoculars and watched the whales with bare eyes.
examples.cn: 他忘了带望远镜，只能用肉眼观看鲸鱼。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oculus 意为眼，bini 意为成双，videre 意为看见。

latinEntries.exampleCN: oculus 产生 ocular 与 binocular。

latinEntries.example: Bini gave the first half of binocular.
latinEntries.exampleCN: bini 构成 binocular 的前半。
videre 产生 video 与 vision。

definition_zh: n. 生物群落（一定生境内相互关联的全部生物）
definition_en: the whole community of living organisms that share a habitat and interact with one another
core_image: 一片浅水里，芦苇、鱼、水鸟和看不见的细菌被同一张网连在一起
scene: 这片湿地里的动植物构成了一个完整的生物群落。The plants and animals of the wetland form a single biocenosis.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：biocenosis 指同一生境内相互关联的全部生物；句意是这片湿地的动植物构成一个完整群落。

senses.title: All the organisms of one habitat
senses.titleCN: 同一生境内的全部生物
senses.definition: the interacting group of plants and animals living together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 在同一地点共同生活的植物与动物的互动集合
senses.example: A pond biocenosis includes reeds, fish, insects and bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘生物群落包括芦苇、鱼类、昆虫和细菌。
senses.why: It was coined in German ecology from bios, life, and koinos, common, for the common living population of a site.
senses.whyCN: 它由德语生态学以 bios（生命）与 koinos（共同）创造，指一处地点共同的生物群体。

senses.title: The living part alone, without its setting
senses.definition: the living community considered separately from the soil, water and climate around it
senses.definitionCN: 把生物群落与周围的土壤、水和气候分开来考虑时的部分
senses.example: In this scheme the biocenosis is the living half and the biotope the physical half.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种划分里，biocenosis 是活的半边，biotope 是物理环境的半边。
senses.why: Ecologists needed a word for the organisms by themselves, because ecosystem names organisms plus their environment.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家需要专指生物本身的词，因为 ecosystem 指生物加环境。

intro.en: Biocenosis is Greek bios, life, plus koinos, common, plus the noun ending -osis.
intro.cn: biocenosis 是希腊语 bios（生命）加 koinos（共同），再接名词词尾 -osis。

items.en: Bios means life, the first element in biology and biography.
items.cn: bios 意为生命，是 biology 与 biography 的第一构件。

items.en: Koinos means common or shared, as in koine, the common Greek.
items.cn: koinos 意为共同、共有，如 koine（共通希腊语）。

items.en: The German ecologist Karl Mobius names the community of organisms.
items.cn: 德国生态学家 Karl Mobius 为这一生物共同体命名。

items.en: The term passes into French and English ecology.
items.cn: 该术语进入法语与英语生态学。

items.en: Biocenosis becomes a standard unit of field study.
items.cn: biocenosis 成为野外研究的标准单位。

items.en: Modern texts often prefer community, but the word survives in ecology.
items.cn: 现代文献多用 community，但该词仍在生态学中沿用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bio- front; the near-meaning group separates the living community from its physical setting and from the larger system that includes both.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bio- 开头；近义组把生物群落与物理环境、以及包含二者的更大系统区分开。

entries.definition: An older spelling of the same term.
Relating to a community of organisms.
The physical space occupied by a community.
entries.definitionCN: 群落所占据的物理空间。

entries.definition: The origin of living things from living things.
Organisms and their surroundings as one system.
entries.definitionCN: 生物与其环境构成的整体系统。

entries.definition: All the species living in one area.
entries.definitionCN: 同一地区内的全部物种。

entries.definition: The natural home of a species.
All living things on the planet together.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上全部生物的整体。

normalIntro.en: Bios is life and koinos is common, so a biocenosis is the common life of one place.
normalIntro.cn: bios 是生命，koinos 是共同，所以 biocenosis 是一处地方共同的生命。

normal.en: Bio- at the front always means life.
normal.cn: 开头的 bio- 永远表示「生命」。

normal.en: Koinos means common, as in the koine Greek of traders.
normal.cn: koinos 意为共同，如商人们通用的 koine 希腊语。

normal.en: Put together: the common life of a habitat.
normal.cn: 合起来：一个生境共同的生命。

normal.en: Reeds, fish, birds and bacteria all belong to one biocenosis.
normal.cn: 芦苇、鱼、鸟和细菌同属一个生物群落。

normal.en: Its physical counterpart is the biotope, the place itself.
normal.cn: 与之相对的物理部分是 biotope，即地点本身。

abstract.en: A net woven out of species.
abstract.cn: 用物种织成的一张网。

abstract.en: One address shared by thousands of lives.
abstract.cn: 成千上万生命共用的同一个地址。

abstract.en: The living half of a landscape.
abstract.cn: 一片景观中「活着」的那一半。

examples.en: The lake biocenosis shifted after the invasive snail arrived.
examples.cn: 入侵螺类到来后，湖泊生物群落发生了变化。

examples.en: Ecologists map a biocenosis before drawing the boundary of a reserve.
examples.cn: 生态学家先给生物群落绘图，再划定保护区边界。

examples.en: The biotope is the stage and the biocenosis is the cast.
examples.cn: biotope 是舞台，biocenosis 是演员。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio 是「生命」，cenosis 让人想到「共聚一处」——一个地方所有生命共同聚在一起，就是生物群落。

root: 希腊 bios（生命）+ koinos（共同）+ -osis（状态、过程）

sensesIntro.en: The word names the living cast of a place; the second sense only makes explicit that the stage itself belongs to another term.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词指一处地方的「活演员」；第二义只是点明舞台本身属于另一个术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reeds, fish, wading birds and invisible bacteria tied together by one shallow pond
core.cn: 核心意象：芦苇、鱼、涉禽与看不见的细菌，被同一片浅水连在一起

branches.en: Bacteria working unseen in the mud.
branches.cn: 在泥中无声工作的细菌。

branches.en: A boundary drawn between life and soil.
branches.cn: 在生命与土壤之间画出的界线。

branches.en: A biotope named separately from its species.
branches.cn: 与物种分开命名的生境。

branches.en: One site split into cast and stage.
branches.cn: 把一处地点分为演员与舞台。

intro.en: Biocenosis is Greek in every part; the list below separates life, commonness and the noun endings that ecology borrows.
intro.cn: biocenosis 各部分都来自希腊语；下面把「生命」「共同」与生态学借用的名词词尾分开。

latinIntro.en: Greek bios is life, koinos is common, and oikos is house, the root of ecology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为生命，koinos 意为共同，oikos 意为家宅，是 ecology 的词根。

latinEntries.exampleCN: bios 产生 biology 与 biocenosis。
koinos 产生 biocenosis 与 koine。
oikos 产生 ecology 与 economy。
